definition_zh: 放弃；抛弃；遗弃；离弃；放任
definition_en: to leave a person, place, or thing behind, or to give up a plan, right, or feeling completely
core_image: 松开的手：原本握住的船缆、人或计划被放下了
scene: 码头在夜里倾斜进海水，缆绳一件件松脱。The crew had to abandon the sinking ship before the deck went under.
sceneCN: 这里 abandon 是「弃置、离开」（第 1 个义项：把某地或某物抛下不管）；句意为船员必须在甲板沉入水中前弃船。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「遗弃；放弃；放任」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「被遗弃的；废弃的」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「遗弃者」

senses.title: To leave a place or thing behind
senses.definition: to leave a place, vehicle, or object behind, especially when it can no longer be used
senses.definitionCN: 把某地、交通工具或物品抛下不管，尤指它已无法继续使用时
senses.example: The crew abandoned the sinking ship.
senses.exampleCN: 船员们弃船而走。
senses.why: The Old French phrase a bandon meant 'at someone's disposal'; putting something there meant giving it up, and a ship left to the sea shows that gesture at its plainest.
senses.whyCN: 古法语短语 a bandon 意为「交由他人处置」；把东西放到那里就是交出，而把船交给大海正是这个动作最直白的模样。

senses.title: To desert a person
senses.definition: to leave a person who depends on you, with no intention of returning
senses.definitionCN: 丢下依赖自己的人，并且没有回来的打算
senses.example: He abandoned his family and moved to another country.
senses.exampleCN: 他抛下家人，搬到了另一个国家。
senses.why: A person can be placed under another's control just as an object can; in this sense the word's old legal image turns into a moral accusation.
senses.whyCN: 人和物品一样可以被「交由他人处置」；在这个义项里，古老的法律意象变成了道德上的指责。

senses.title: To give up a plan
senses.definition: to stop working on a plan, project, or course of action before it is finished
senses.definitionCN: 在计划、项目或行动方案完成之前停止推进
senses.example: The company abandoned the plan when the costs doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 成本翻倍后，公司放弃了这个计划。
senses.why: A plan is something held in the hand; letting go of it is the same release, only the object is now an intention rather than a thing.
senses.whyCN: 计划是握在手里的东西；放开它还是同一个松手动作，只不过对象从实物变成了意图。

senses.title: To forsake a belief
senses.definition: to stop supporting or believing in an idea, cause, or principle
senses.definitionCN: 不再支持或相信某个理念、事业或原则
senses.example: She never abandoned her belief in public education.
senses.exampleCN: 她从未放弃对公共教育的信念。
senses.why: Beliefs are held like possessions and can be put down in public; the old sense of a formal declaration survives in this grave, deliberate use.
senses.whyCN: 信念像财产一样被持有，也可以当众放下；这个郑重而深思的用法里，仍留着「公开声明交出」的古老意味。

senses.title: To leave a post or duty
senses.definition: to leave a position or responsibility that one is expected to keep
senses.definitionCN: 离开本应坚守的职位或责任
senses.example: The guard abandoned his post during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨中，卫兵擅离了岗位。
senses.why: A post is a place one is tied to; abandoning it is cutting that tie without permission, which is why the word carries blame here.
senses.whyCN: 岗位是人与之系在一起的位置；擅离就是未经允许切断这根绳子，所以这个义项带着责难。

senses.title: To give oneself over to a feeling
senses.definition: to let a feeling or activity take complete control of you
senses.definitionCN: 让某种情绪或活动完全支配自己
senses.example: He abandoned himself to grief after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后，他沉浸在悲痛之中。
senses.why: To abandon oneself is to hand control to something else, exactly as a bandon handed a thing to another's power; here the new owner is an emotion.
senses.whyCN: abandon oneself 就是把控制权交给别的东西，正如 a bandon 把物品交给他人支配；只不过这里的新主人是一种情绪。

senses.title: To give up hope
senses.definition: to stop expecting that something good will happen
senses.definitionCN: 不再期待好事会发生
senses.example: Rescuers refused to abandon hope after the third day.
senses.exampleCN: 第三天之后，救援人员仍拒绝放弃希望。
senses.why: Hope is the last thing people hold when everything else is gone; dropping it repeats the core gesture at its most absolute.
senses.whyCN: 当其他一切都失去时，希望是人最后握着的东西；放下它就是把这个核心动作做到最彻底。

senses.title: To stop using a practice
senses.definition: to stop using a method, system, or practice and leave it behind
senses.definitionCN: 停止使用某种方法、制度或做法，把它留在过去
senses.example: The school abandoned the old grading system last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校去年停止了旧的评分制度。
senses.why: An outdated practice is treated as an empty building: people move out and it is left standing, unused.
senses.whyCN: 过时的做法被当作空置的房屋：人们搬走，把它留在原地不再使用。

intro.en: Abandon reached English through French, and its earliest image is not a ship but a phrase about handing something over.
intro.cn: abandon 经由法语进入英语，它最早的意象不是船，而是一个表示「交出处置权」的短语。

items.en: The reconstructed Frankish word *bann meant 'proclamation, command, authority'. The reconstruction is generally accepted but the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 重构的法兰克语词 *bann 意为「公告、命令、权威」；这一重构一般被接受，但确切形式不确定。

items.en: In the phrase a bandon, bandon meant 'power, disposal'; a bandon therefore meant 'at another's disposal'.
items.cn: 在短语 a bandon 中，bandon 意为「支配权、处置权」；因此 a bandon 表示「任凭他人处置」。

items.en: abandonner developed the sense 'to put under another's control' and then 'to give up, desert'.
items.cn: abandonner 发展出「交由他人控制」之义，随后又得到「放弃、抛弃」的意思。

items.en: The verb appears in English in the fourteenth century as abandounen; the precise first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪以 abandounen 的形式出现在英语中；确切的首次记录年代不确定。

items.en: Later usage stretches from ships and places to people, plans, beliefs, posts, and finally to emotions and hope.
items.cn: 后来的用法从船只和地点扩展到人、计划、信念、岗位，最后扩展到情绪与希望。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adjective, and one modern compound from the same family; the second gathers verbs of leaving or giving up.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的名称、形容词与一个现代复合词；第二组收表示丢下或交出的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or state of being left behind or given up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗弃、放弃」，指被抛下或交出的行为或状态。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a person, place, or thing that has been left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被遗弃的、废弃的」，描述被抛下的人、地方或物品。

entries.definition: Software that its owner no longer sells or supports but that users still circulate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「弃置软件」，指厂商已停止销售与支持、用户仍在传播的软件。

entries.definition: The Old French noun meaning 'power or disposal' that survives inside the English verb.
entries.definitionCN: 古法语名词，义为「支配权、处置权」，只保留在英语动词的构词痕迹中。

entries.definition: To leave a person or place in a way that is seen as a betrayal of duty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抛弃、遗弃」，带着背弃责任的意味离开某人或某地。

entries.definition: To give up someone or something once cared for, often in a solemn or literary tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「舍弃、抛弃」，多用于郑重或文学语气，指放弃曾珍视的人或物。

entries.definition: To give up a right, position, or possession, usually formally and reluctantly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「放弃、让出」，通常指正式而不情愿地交出权利、职位或财物。

entries.definition: To get rid of or leave someone or something abruptly, in informal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，非正式用法，义为「甩掉、丢下」，突然抛弃某人或某物。

entries.definition: To throw cargo or equipment off a ship or aircraft to lighten it, or to discard an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抛弃、投弃」，指为减重把货物或设备抛下船机，也指丢弃某个想法。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks come from the French phrase behind the word, its fixed maritime collocation, and its noun family; the abstract hooks turn the release into pictures.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点来自词后的法语短语、固定的航海搭配与名词词族；抽象记忆点把「松手」变成画面。

normal.en: a bandon in Old French meant 'at someone's disposal'; to abandon was to put something there.
normal.cn: 古法语 a bandon 意为「任凭处置」；abandon 就是把人或物放到那个位置。

normal.en: Abandon ship is a fixed order at sea, which fixes the verb in memory.
normal.cn: Abandon ship 是海上固定口令，能把这个动词牢牢记住。

normal.en: Abandonment is the noun, and abandoned is the adjective for what has been left.
normal.cn: 名词是 abandonment，形容词 abandoned 表示「被遗弃的」。

normal.en: Abandon hope is a set phrase, as in the line about leaving hope behind.
normal.cn: abandon hope 是固定说法，常见于「把希望留在身后」一类的句子。

normal.en: Abandon oneself to joy or grief means handing control to that feeling.
normal.cn: 「abandon oneself to joy or grief」意为把控制权交给那种情绪。

abstract.en: Picture a rope slipping out of an open hand into dark water.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子从张开的手里滑落，掉进黑水里。

abstract.en: Picture a house with its door open and its lights off, still full of furniture nobody uses.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋门开着、灯灭着的房子，家具还在，却没人再用。

abstract.en: Picture a runner dropping a heavy pack at the roadside and walking on without looking back.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者把沉重的背包丢在路边，头也不回地继续走。

examples.en: They abandoned the car when the road flooded.
examples.cn: 道路被淹后，他们丢下了那辆车。

examples.en: The minister refused to abandon the reform.
examples.cn: 部长拒绝放弃这项改革。

examples.en: The village was abandoned after the mine closed.
examples.cn: 矿场关闭后，村庄被废弃了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额班登」——像把行李往地上一放、人转身就走，东西就留在了原地。

root: 法语 a bandon（任凭处置）+ 动词后缀 -er，经古法语 abandonner 进入英语；核心义是「把人或物交出去、不再管」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from leaving an object, to leaving people and obligations, to surrendering plans and beliefs, and finally to handing oneself over to a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从抛下物品，走到抛下人与义务，再到交出计划与信念，最后是把自己交给一种情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand letting go of what it held
core.cn: 核心意象：张开的手放开原本握住的东西

branches.en: Physical release: a ship, car, building, or practice is left behind and no longer used.
branches.cn: 实物的放手：船、车、建筑或做法被留在原地，不再使用。

branches.en: Human desertion: people and posts are left without care or permission.
branches.cn: 对人的抛弃：人被丢下无人照管，岗位被擅自离开。

branches.en: Giving up intentions: plans and beliefs are dropped before they are finished.
branches.cn: 交出意图：计划与信念在完成之前被放下。

branches.en: Surrender of the self: control is handed to an emotion.
branches.cn: 自我的交出：控制权被交给一种情绪。

branches.en: Absolute release: even hope is let go.
branches.cn: 彻底的放手：连希望也被放下。

intro.en: The word is built from a French phrase rather than from a Latin prefix, so the useful pieces are the French a-, the noun suffix -ment, and the adjective and agent endings.
intro.cn: 这个词由法语短语而非拉丁前缀构成，因此有用的构件是法语前缀 a-、名词后缀 -ment，以及形容词与施动者后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no direct Latin ancestor; the closest Latin-family records are Medieval Latin words for a ban or a proclamation, borrowed from the same Frankish root.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有直接的拉丁语祖先；最接近的拉丁词族记录是中世纪拉丁语中表示「禁令、公告」的词，同样借自那个法兰克语词根。

items.meaning: to, toward; here a weakened form of Latin ad-
items.meaningCN: 向、朝；此处是拉丁语 ad- 的弱化形式
items.exampleCN: abandonner 进入英语后写作 abandon

items.meaningCN: 完成的行为或由此形成的状态

items.meaning: a person who does the action
goods or products of a kind
present tense with he, she, or it

items.example: the root of bandon and ban
items.exampleCN: bandon 与 ban 的共同词根

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「遗弃；放弃」
形容词，义为「被遗弃的；废弃的」

definition_zh: 减弱；减退；缓解；降低；废除
definition_en: to become less strong, intense, or numerous, or to make something less so
core_image: 正在退去的潮水：水位一点点往下落
scene: 暴雨敲了一整夜，天快亮时风声渐渐松了下来。By morning the storm had abated and the streets were quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 abate 是「强度减弱」（第 1 个义项：风暴等自然力量变弱）；句意为到早晨风暴已经减弱，街道安静下来。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「减弱；减免；废止」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「未减弱的；不减的」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「减轻者；消除者」

senses.title: Of a storm: to become weaker
senses.definition: of wind, rain, or a storm, to lose force
senses.definitionCN: 指风、雨或风暴失去力量
senses.example: The storm abated before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明前风暴减弱了。
senses.why: The Old French verb abatre meant 'to beat down'; a storm that is beaten down loses its force, and the image survives in every later use.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 abatre 意为「打下去」；被压下去的风暴失去力量，这个意象一直留到后来的所有用法里。

senses.title: Of pain or fever: to subside
senses.definition: of pain, fever, or a symptom, to become less severe
senses.definitionCN: 指疼痛、发烧或症状变得不那么严重
senses.example: The fever abated after the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 服药之后，发烧退了。
senses.why: Illness is pictured as a force pressing on the body; when that pressure is beaten down, the symptom subsides.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被想象成压在身体上的一股力量；这股压力被压下去，症状也就减轻了。

senses.title: Of anger: to cool down
senses.definition: of anger, excitement, or tension, to become calmer
senses.definitionCN: 指怒气、激动或紧张变得平静
senses.example: His anger abated once he heard the full story.
senses.exampleCN: 听完完整经过后，他的怒气平息了。
senses.why: Emotions rise like weather; the same verb that describes a dying storm describes a temper losing its heat.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像天气一样升起；描述风暴渐息的那个动词，也同样描述脾气退热。

senses.title: Of numbers: to decrease
senses.definition: to fall in amount, rate, or number
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、比率或数目上下降
senses.example: Inflation showed no sign of abating.
senses.exampleCN: 通胀没有任何减弱的迹象。
senses.why: From wind and fever the word extends to anything measurable that rises too high and then comes down.
senses.whyCN: 从风与发烧，这个词扩展到任何升得过高、随后回落的可测量事物。

senses.title: To reduce a charge
senses.definition: to make a rent, tax, or charge smaller
senses.definitionCN: 使租金、税款或费用变少
senses.example: The landlord agreed to abate the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房东同意减免租金。
senses.why: A charge is a burden laid on someone; abating it is beating that burden down to a lighter weight.
senses.whyCN: 费用是压在某人身上的负担；abate 就是把这副担子打下去、减轻重量。

senses.title: Legal: to remove a nuisance
senses.definition: to end or remove a nuisance, especially by legal order
senses.definitionCN: 终止或消除妨害，尤指依法律命令
senses.example: The court ordered the factory to abate the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令工厂消除噪音。
senses.why: A nuisance is a harm that keeps pressing on a neighbourhood; the law uses the old beating image to say that the harm must be pushed down.
senses.whyCN: 妨害是持续压在社区上的一种损害；法律借用古老的「打压」意象，表示必须把这股损害压下去。

senses.title: Legal: to quash a writ
senses.definition: to render a legal writ or action void
senses.definitionCN: 使某项令状或法律诉讼失效
senses.example: The writ was abated when the defendant died.
senses.exampleCN: 被告死亡后，令状被废止。
senses.why: In law the image turns administrative: an action that can no longer stand is beaten down and declared void.
senses.whyCN: 在法律里，这个意象转为程序性的：无法继续的诉讼被压下去，宣告失效。

senses.title: To lessen something
senses.definition: to make pressure, risk, or intensity less
senses.definitionCN: 使压力、风险或强度变小
senses.example: The new policy abated the pressure on hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策减轻了医院的压力。
senses.why: The transitive use simply puts the same beating action into someone's hands: an agent lowers the force instead of waiting for it to fall.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法只是把同样的「打压」动作交到某人手里：由人主动降低力量，而不是等它自己落下。

intro.en: Abate comes from a French verb meaning 'to beat down', which goes back to the Latin verb for beating.
intro.cn: abate 来自一个意为「打下去」的法语动词，后者可追溯到表示「打」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: battuere meant 'to beat, strike'; it also lies behind English battle and battery.
items.cn: battuere 意为「打、击」，英语 battle 与 battery 也源自它。

items.en: A reconstructed compound of ad- 'to' and battuere gave the sense 'to beat down'; the form is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: 由 ad-（向）与 battuere 构成的重构词，得到「打下去」之义；这一形式是重构的，并非实际文献所载。

items.en: abatre meant 'to knock down, fell, destroy', and its figurative sense 'to lessen' was already present.
items.cn: abatre 意为「击倒、砍倒、摧毁」，其比喻义「减弱」当时已经存在。

items.en: English abaten is recorded from the fourteenth century with the sense 'to diminish'.
items.cn: 英语 abaten 自十四世纪有记录，意为「减少、减弱」。

items.en: Medical and legal senses were added later, including the abatement of a nuisance or a writ.
items.cn: 医学与法律义项是后来增加的，包括消除妨害与废止令状。

note.en: The first group gathers words sharing the Latin verb for beating; the second gathers verbs for things becoming smaller or weaker.
note.cn: 第一组收共享拉丁语「打」这一动词的词；第二组收表示事物变小变弱的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a reduction in strength, amount, or a legal charge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「减弱、减少、减免」，指强度、数量或费用的降低。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning that something continues without any reduction.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未减弱的」，表示某事毫无减弱地持续。

entries.definition: A partial refund; it comes from the same French verb for beating something back.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「折扣、退款」，同样来自那个表示「打回去」的法语动词。

entries.definition: A set of connected cells, or the act of beating; both go back to Latin battuere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电池组」或「殴打」，二者都可追溯到拉丁语 battuere。

entries.definition: A formal discussion; it shares the beating root through the idea of striking words together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「辩论」，经由「话语交锋」的观念共享同一个「打」的词根。

entries.definition: Of a storm, flood, or feeling, to sink to a lower level.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「平息、退去」，指风暴、洪水或情绪降到较低水平。

entries.definition: To become or make smaller in size, amount, or importance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「减少、缩小」，指在大小、数量或重要性上变小。

entries.definition: To reduce in degree or extent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「减轻、减少」，指在程度或范围上降低。

entries.definition: To become gradually smaller or weaker over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「逐渐减少」，指随时间慢慢变小或变弱。

entries.definition: Of tides or energy, to flow back and decline.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「退潮、衰退」，指潮水或精力退回、减弱。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the legal collocation, the storm image, and the noun family; the abstract hooks turn the falling water level into three pictures.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用法律搭配、风暴意象与名词词族；抽象记忆点把下落的水位化成三幅画面。

normal.en: Abate a nuisance is a standard legal phrase for removing a harmful condition.
normal.cn: abate a nuisance 是标准法律短语，表示消除有害状况。

normal.en: A storm abates; the same verb appears in weather reports and in news about inflation.
normal.cn: 风暴会 abate；同一个动词也出现在天气播报和通胀新闻里。

normal.en: Unabated means the force never dropped, as in 'the storm continued unabated'.
normal.cn: unabated 表示力量从未下降，如「风暴持续不减」。

normal.en: Abatement is the noun, common in rent abatement and noise abatement.
normal.cn: 名词 abatement 常见于减租与降噪的说法中。

normal.en: The -ate ending marks a verb, and the French source verb meant to beat down.
normal.cn: -ate 结尾标明动词，法语来源动词意为「打下去」。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pulling back from a stone pier, leaving the steps dry.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水从石码头退去，把台阶留在干燥处。

abstract.en: Picture a flame turned down by a knob until it is only a blue ring.
abstract.cn: 想象火焰被旋钮调小，只剩一圈蓝光。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd's noise thinning out until the hall is almost silent.
abstract.cn: 想象人群的喧闹渐渐稀疏，直到大厅几乎无声。

examples.en: The wind abated just after sunset.
examples.cn: 日落之后风就减弱了。

examples.en: Nothing could abate her grief.
examples.cn: 什么都无法减轻她的悲伤。

examples.en: The council moved to abate noise from the highway.
examples.cn: 市议会着手降低高速公路的噪音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额贝特」——像把音量键往下拨，额度一格格变小，声音就轻了。

root: 古法语 abatre（击倒、打下去），源自拉丁语 battuere（打）+ ad-（向）；核心义是「把力量打下去」

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from physical forces losing strength, through body and emotion, to measurable amounts and to legal actions that are cancelled.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从自然力量失去强度，经过身体与情绪，走到可计量的数量，最后是被撤销的法律行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: floodwater dropping down the marked steps of a pier
core.cn: 核心意象：洪水沿着码头刻度的台阶一层层退落

branches.en: Natural and bodily pressure falls away: storm, fever, and anger all lose heat.
branches.cn: 自然与身体的压力退去：风暴、发烧与怒气都失去热度。

branches.en: Measurable quantities fall: rates, numbers, and levels come down.
branches.cn: 可计量的数量下降：比率、数目与水平回落。

branches.en: A burden is made lighter by an agent: charges are cut and pressure is eased.
branches.cn: 人主动减轻负担：费用被减免，压力被缓解。

branches.en: A harmful condition is removed by legal order.
branches.cn: 依法律命令消除有害状况。

branches.en: A legal action is cancelled and declared void.
branches.cn: 法律行为被撤销并宣告失效。

intro.en: The family is held together by the French stem bat- 'to beat', with prefixes and suffixes that mark negation, result, and agent.
intro.cn: 这个词族由法语词干 bat-（打）连在一起，前缀与后缀分别标记否定、结果与施动者。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source verb battuere also produced battle, battery, and combat, so the Latin entries record the shared root rather than a direct ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源动词 battuere 还生出 battle、battery、combat，因此拉丁条目记录的是共享词根，而非直接祖先。

items.meaning: present tense with he, she, or it

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「减弱；减免；废止」
形容词，义为「未减弱的；不减的」

definition_zh: 腹部；腹腔；（昆虫、甲壳类的）腹部
definition_en: the part of the body between the chest and the pelvis, or the rear section of an insect's or crustacean's body
core_image: 躯干中段那个装着肠胃的柔软腔体
scene: 医生先让病人平躺，再轻轻按压腹部寻找痛点。The surgeon pressed gently on her abdomen to locate the source of the pain.
sceneCN: 这里 abdomen 是「腹部」（第 1 个义项：人体胸部与骨盆之间的区域）；句意为外科医生轻按她的腹部，寻找疼痛的来源。

pos.zh: 昆虫或甲壳动物的腹部体段

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「腹部的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「在腹部；按腹部方式」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「大腹的；肥胖的」
由本词与表示「成形术」的成分构成，义为「腹壁整形术」

senses.title: The human belly region
senses.definition: the front part of the body between the chest and the hips, containing the stomach and intestines
senses.definitionCN: 人体胸部与髋部之间的前部区域，内有胃与肠
senses.example: He felt a sharp pain in his abdomen after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后他感到腹部一阵剧痛。
senses.why: Latin abdomen named the belly as a whole; the word entered medical English as the neutral term for the region that holds the digestive organs.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abdomen 整体指「肚子」；这个词作为中性术语进入医学英语，指容纳消化器官的区域。

senses.title: The abdominal cavity
senses.definition: the space inside the body that contains the stomach, intestines, liver, and other organs
senses.definitionCN: 体内容纳胃、肠、肝等器官的空间
senses.example: The scan showed fluid in the abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示腹腔内有积液。
senses.why: Once the outer belly is named, the same word is extended inward to the cavity behind it.
senses.whyCN: 外部腹部有了名称之后，同一个词又被向内延伸到它后面的腔体。

senses.title: The insect abdomen
senses.definition: the third and rear section of an insect's body, behind the thorax
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫身体第三节，位于胸部之后
senses.example: The wasp's sting sits at the tip of its abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 黄蜂的刺长在腹部的末端。
senses.why: Entomology borrowed the human term for the rear body segment because it also holds the gut.
senses.whyCN: 昆虫学借用了人体术语来指后部体段，因为那里同样容纳肠道。

senses.title: The crustacean abdomen
senses.definition: the segmented rear part of a crustacean such as a shrimp or crab
senses.definitionCN: 虾或蟹等甲壳动物分节的躯干后部
senses.example: The shrimp flexed its abdomen to propel itself backward.
senses.exampleCN: 虾弯曲腹部，把自己向后推。
senses.why: In arthropods the same body plan repeats, so the belly word naturally covers the tail-like rear section.
senses.whyCN: 节肢动物的身体结构彼此相似，因此这个「肚子」的词自然也能指像尾巴一样的后段。

senses.title: The arachnid abdomen
senses.definition: the rear body part of a spider or similar animal, which contains the digestive and reproductive organs
senses.definitionCN: 蜘蛛等动物躯干的后部，内含消化与生殖器官
senses.example: The spider's abdomen is often larger than its front body.
senses.exampleCN: 蜘蛛的腹部往往比前体更大。
senses.why: The term is a general anatomical label for the hind body, whatever the species.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语是所有物种后部躯体的通用解剖标签。

senses.title: A paunch
senses.definition: a rounded or fat belly, used in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中指圆鼓或肥胖的肚子
senses.example: He patted his abdomen and laughed about his diet.
senses.exampleCN: 他拍拍自己的肚腩，笑谈起节食。
senses.why: The neutral medical word is softened into a friendly or teasing reference to a large belly.
senses.whyCN: 中性的医学词被软化，用来友善或打趣地指肥大的肚子。

senses.title: Acute abdomen
senses.definition: a medical condition of sudden severe abdominal pain that may need surgery
senses.definitionCN: 突发剧烈腹痛、可能需要手术的医学状况
senses.example: The patient was admitted with an acute abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 病人因急腹症入院。
senses.why: A body region becomes a clinical label: the abdomen itself signals the emergency.
senses.whyCN: 一个身体区域变成了临床标签：腹部本身就在提示急症。

senses.title: The lower trunk of a vertebrate
senses.definition: the lower trunk region of a vertebrate animal, between the rib cage and the pelvis
senses.definitionCN: 脊椎动物肋骨与骨盆之间的躯干下部区域
senses.example: The frog's abdomen is pale and smooth.
senses.exampleCN: 青蛙的腹部苍白而光滑。
senses.why: Comparative anatomy uses the same term across vertebrates, keeping the meaning close to the original Latin belly.
senses.whyCN: 比较解剖学在各类脊椎动物中沿用同一个词，含义贴近拉丁语原义「肚子」。

intro.en: Abdomen is a Latin anatomical word of uncertain origin; it may be linked to the verb 'to hide', because the belly hides the organs.
intro.cn: abdomen 是一个来源不确定的拉丁语解剖词；它可能与表示「藏起来」的动词有关，因为肚子把器官藏在里面。

items.en: No agreed Indo-European root has been reconstructed for abdomen; the deeper history of the word is source uncertain.
items.cn: abdomen 尚无可公认的原始印欧语词根；这个词更深层的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin abdomen meant 'belly'. One common suggestion links it to abdere 'to hide', but this is a hypothesis, not an established fact.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abdomen 意为「肚子」。一种常见推测把它与 abdere（藏起来）联系起来，但这只是假说，并非定论。

items.en: The adjective abdominalis already existed in Latin medical writing.
items.cn: 形容词 abdominalis 在拉丁医学文献中已经存在。

items.en: French medical texts adopted abdomen in the sixteenth century as a learned term.
items.cn: 十六世纪的法语医学文献把这个词作为学术术语吸收进来。

items.en: English anatomy books took the word from Latin and French, keeping its neutral clinical tone.
items.cn: 英语解剖学著作从拉丁语和法语借入该词，保留了它中性、临床的语气。

items.en: Later biology extended it to insects and crustaceans, whose rear body segment is also called the abdomen.
items.cn: 后来的生物学把它扩展到昆虫与甲壳动物，它们后部的体段同样称作腹部。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective and related medical forms; the second gathers everyday words for the belly.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词与相关医学形式；第二组收日常表示肚子的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of or relating to the abdomen'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「腹部的；与腹部有关的」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in the abdomen or by means of the abdomen'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在腹部；以腹部方式」。

entries.definition: An adjective, now rare, meaning 'having a large belly'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，现已罕见，义为「大腹的；肥胖的」。

entries.definition: Cosmetic surgery that removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「腹壁整形术」，指切除腹部多余皮肤与脂肪的整形手术。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the front of the body below the chest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肚子」，是胸部以下身体前部的日常说法。

entries.definition: The organ that receives food, often used loosely for the whole belly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胃」，也常宽松地指整个腹部。

entries.definition: A child-friendly or informal word for the belly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小肚肚」，是童语或非正式说法。

entries.definition: A large, often protruding belly, especially in an older man.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大肚腩」，尤指年长男性突出的肚子。

entries.definition: The intestines or the belly as a whole, used informally.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，非正式用法，义为「肠子」或整个腹部。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks work from the anatomical collocations and the family of adjectives; the abstract hooks picture the soft middle of the body.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点来自解剖搭配与形容词词族；抽象记忆点想象身体中段那个柔软的腔体。

normal.en: Lower abdomen and upper abdomen divide the belly into two clinical zones.
normal.cn: lower abdomen 与 upper abdomen 把肚子分成两个临床区域。

normal.en: Acute abdomen is the emergency label for sudden severe belly pain.
normal.cn: acute abdomen 是突发剧烈腹痛的急症标签。

normal.en: Abdominal is the adjective, as in abdominal muscles.
normal.cn: 形容词是 abdominal，如 abdominal muscles（腹部肌肉）。

normal.en: Abdominoplasty joins abdomen with the suffix for surgical reshaping.
normal.cn: abdominoplasty 把 abdomen 与表示外科整形的后缀组合起来。

normal.en: Insects and crabs also have an abdomen, because the word names the rear body section.
normal.cn: 昆虫和蟹也有 abdomen，因为这个词指后部体段。

abstract.en: Picture a soft pouch tied around the middle of the body, holding the stomach and intestines.
abstract.cn: 想象身体中段系着一个柔软的袋子，里面装着胃和肠。

abstract.en: Picture an insect drawn as three beads, with the last bead called the abdomen.
abstract.cn: 想象昆虫画成三颗珠子，最后一颗叫腹部。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor's two fingers pressing a patient's belly to find the sore spot.
abstract.cn: 想象医生的两根手指按在病人肚子上，寻找痛点。

examples.en: The pain began in the lower abdomen.
examples.cn: 疼痛从下腹部开始。

examples.en: A bee's abdomen is striped black and yellow.
examples.cn: 蜜蜂的腹部有黑黄条纹。

examples.en: The scan revealed a small mass in his abdomen.
examples.cn: 扫描发现他腹腔里有一个小结节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布多门」——肚子像一扇门，里面藏着肠胃，门外只看见柔软的腹部。

root: 拉丁语 abdomen（肚子），来源不确定；一种推测与 abdere（藏起来）有关，因为腹部把内脏藏在其后

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with the human belly and its inner cavity, then spread to insects, crustaceans, and spiders, and finally to everyday and clinical uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从人的腹部与腹腔开始，扩展到昆虫、甲壳类与蜘蛛，最后落到日常与临床用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the soft middle chamber that holds the gut
core.cn: 核心意象：装着肠子的柔软中段腔体

branches.en: The human and vertebrate belly, seen from outside or as an inner cavity.
branches.cn: 人与脊椎动物的腹部，可从外部看，也可指内部腔体。

branches.en: The rear body section of arthropods, named by analogy with the gut-holding belly.
branches.cn: 节肢动物的后部体段，因同样容纳肠道而与人的腹部类比得名。

branches.en: The rounded everyday belly, often mentioned with a smile.
branches.cn: 日常中圆鼓的肚子，常带笑谈语气。

branches.en: The lower trunk as a comparative-anatomy region.
branches.cn: 作为比较解剖学区域的躯干下部。

branches.en: The clinical label for a sudden abdominal emergency.
branches.cn: 用于突发腹部急症的临床标签。

intro.en: The useful pieces are the Latin stem abdomin- and the adjective and adverb endings that build the medical family.
intro.cn: 有用的构件是拉丁词干 abdomin-，以及构成医学词族的形容词与副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective abdominalis is the direct source of the English adjective, so the Latin entries record the same stem in its original endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 abdominalis 是英语形容词的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录的是同一词干在拉丁语中的词尾形式。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「腹部的」
名词，义为「腹壁整形术」

definition_zh: 诱拐；绑架；（解剖学）外展；（逻辑）溯因推理
definition_en: the act of taking someone away by force or deception, or the movement of a limb away from the body
core_image: 一只手把人和物从原来的位置带走
scene: 监控里，一名男子抱起街边的孩子就上了车。Police launched an investigation into the abduction of a young boy.
sceneCN: 这里 abduction 是「诱拐、绑架」（第 1 个义项：非法带走他人）；句意为警方对一名男孩被诱拐展开调查。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀构成，义为「诱拐；绑架；使外展」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「诱拐者；绑架者；外展肌」
由动词加表示被动者的后缀构成，义为「被绑架者；被诱拐者」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「溯因的；诱拐的」

senses.title: Taking a child away
senses.definition: the illegal taking away of a child, often by deception or force
senses.definitionCN: 以欺骗或暴力非法带走儿童
senses.example: The abduction of the child was caught on camera.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子被诱拐的过程被摄像头拍了下来。
senses.why: Latin abducere meant 'to lead away'; the noun abductio named the act of carrying someone off, and the criminal sense grew from that plain image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abducere 意为「带走」；名词 abductio 指把人带离的行为，犯罪义项正是从这个朴素意象发展出来的。

senses.title: Kidnapping an adult
senses.definition: the act of seizing and carrying off an adult against their will
senses.definitionCN: 违背成人意愿将其抓住并带走
senses.example: The gang was convicted of the abduction of a businessman.
senses.exampleCN: 该团伙因绑架一名商人而被定罪。
senses.why: The same leading-away action applies to adults; the word stresses the carrying off rather than the ransom.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「带离」动作也适用于成人；这个词强调的是带走本身，而非赎金。

senses.title: Anatomical abduction
senses.definition: the movement of a limb or body part away from the midline of the body
senses.definitionCN: 肢体或身体部位离开身体中线的动作
senses.example: The therapist tested shoulder abduction through its full range.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师完整测试了肩关节外展的活动范围。
senses.why: Anatomists reused the Latin verb for leading away: the limb is led away from the body's centre line.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学家沿用了这个表示「带走」的拉丁动词：肢体被带离身体中线。

senses.title: Abductive reasoning
senses.definition: a form of reasoning that infers the most likely explanation for an observation
senses.definitionCN: 为某个观察推断最可能解释的推理形式
senses.example: Detectives rely on abduction when they form a hypothesis from clues.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探根据线索提出假设时，依靠的正是溯因推理。
senses.why: Logic borrowed the term for 'leading away' because the mind is led away from the observed fact to a possible cause behind it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学借用了「带走」这个词，因为思维被从观察到的事实带向其背后可能的原因。

senses.title: Unlawful taking in law
senses.definition: the legal charge for taking a person away unlawfully, especially a minor
senses.definitionCN: 法律上非法带走他人、尤指未成年人的罪名
senses.example: The court treated the case as abduction rather than a custody dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把此案按诱拐处理，而非监护权纠纷。
senses.why: The law adopts the plain 'leading away' image and fixes it to a charge, so the act itself names the offence.
senses.whyCN: 法律采用「带走」这个朴素意象并把它固定为一项罪名，于是行为本身就成了罪名的名称。

senses.title: Carrying off young animals
senses.definition: the taking away of young animals from their group or parent
senses.definitionCN: 把幼崽从其群体或亲代身边带走
senses.example: Researchers recorded the abduction of a cub by a rival male.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员记录了一头幼崽被敌对雄性带走的情况。
senses.why: Field biology applies the human term to animals when one animal carries off another's young.
senses.whyCN: 野外生物学把人的术语用于动物，指一只动物带走另一只的幼崽。

senses.title: Muscle action of abducting
senses.definition: the action of a muscle that pulls a limb away from the midline
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉把肢体拉离中线的动作
senses.example: The abductor muscle performs abduction of the little finger.
senses.exampleCN: 外展肌完成小指的外展动作。
senses.why: The movement sense is narrowed to the muscle that produces it, so the noun can name the action of a specific muscle.
senses.whyCN: 动作义被收窄到产生它的肌肉上，因此这个名词也能指某块肌肉的具体动作。

senses.title: Alien abduction
senses.definition: a claimed case in which aliens take a person away, usually temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 声称外星人把人带走、通常短暂带离的说法
senses.example: The witness described an alleged alien abduction.
senses.exampleCN: 证人描述了一次据称的外星人绑架。
senses.why: Popular culture stretches the criminal image into science fiction, where the kidnappers come from the sky.
senses.whyCN: 流行文化把犯罪意象延伸到科幻领域，绑架者来自天上。

intro.en: Abduction goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to lead away', built from a prefix of separation and the verb for leading.
intro.cn: abduction 可追溯到意为「带走」的拉丁语动词，由表示分离的前缀与表示「引导」的动词构成。

items.en: The root *deuk- is reconstructed with the sense 'to lead'; it also lies behind duke and duct.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *deuk- 被重构为「引导」之义；duke 与 duct 也源自它。

items.en: ducere meant 'to lead, draw'; it produced a large family including ductus and dux.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」，衍生出 ductus、dux 等一大批词。

items.en: ab- 'away' plus ducere formed abducere, 'to lead away, carry off'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 ducere 构成 abducere，意为「带走、领走」。

items.en: The noun abductio named the act of leading away, including in anatomical writing.
items.cn: 名词 abductio 指带走的行为，解剖学文献中也有此用法。

items.en: English adopted abduction for the criminal sense and for the anatomical movement.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪吸收该词，用于犯罪义项与解剖学动作。

items.en: Logic added the sense of inference to the best explanation, and popular culture added alien abduction.
items.cn: 逻辑学补充了「最佳解释推断」之义，流行文化又补充了「外星人绑架」之义。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, the person who acts, the person acted upon, and the adjective; the second gathers words for taking a person away.
note.cn: 第一组收动词、施动者、被施动者与形容词；第二组收表示把人带走的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to take someone away or to move a limb outward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「诱拐、绑架」或「使肢体外展」。

entries.definition: A person who carries someone off, or a muscle that moves a limb away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「诱拐者」或「外展肌」。

entries.definition: The person who has been taken away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「被绑架者、被诱拐者」。

entries.definition: An adjective describing reasoning that infers a likely explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「溯因的」，描述推断可能解释的推理。

entries.definition: The crime of seizing a person and holding them, often for ransom.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绑架」，指抓走并扣押他人、常为索要赎金的罪行。

entries.definition: A quick, sudden taking away, often of a bag or a child.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「抢夺、迅速抓走」，常指抢包或抱走孩子。

entries.definition: The act of taking hold of someone or something by force.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「夺取、扣押」，指以武力抓住人或物。

entries.definition: The taking control of a vehicle or aircraft by force.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「劫持」，指以武力控制交通工具。

entries.definition: The act of catching and holding a person or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「捕获、俘获」，指抓住并扣留人或动物。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin pieces, the anatomical pairing, and the criminal collocations; the abstract hooks picture the carrying away.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁构件、解剖学配对与犯罪搭配；抽象记忆点想象「带走」的动作。

normal.en: ab- means away and ducere means to lead, so abduction is literally a leading away.
normal.cn: ab- 表示离开，ducere 表示引导，因此 abduction 字面就是「带走」。

normal.en: Abduction and adduction are a pair: away from the midline and toward it.
normal.cn: abduction 与 adduction 是一对：一个离开中线，一个靠向中线。

normal.en: Child abduction and attempted abduction are common news collocations.
normal.cn: child abduction 与 attempted abduction 是常见新闻搭配。

normal.en: The abductor takes the abductee; the two endings keep the roles apart.
normal.cn: abductor 带走 abductee；两个后缀把施动者与受动者区分开。

normal.en: Abductive reasoning is the logic sense, inferring the best explanation.
normal.cn: abductive reasoning 是逻辑义，指推断最佳解释。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing on a small figure and pulling it out of the frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抓住一个小小的人影，把它拉出画面。

abstract.en: Picture an arm lifting sideways, away from the centre line of the body.
abstract.cn: 想象一条手臂向侧面抬起，离开身体中线。

abstract.en: Picture a detective staring at footprints and following them back to a hidden door.
abstract.cn: 想象侦探盯着脚印，顺着它追到一扇隐藏的门。

examples.en: The police are investigating the abduction.
examples.cn: 警方正在调查这起绑架案。

examples.en: The doctor measured abduction of the shoulder.
examples.cn: 医生测量了肩关节的外展幅度。

examples.en: The theory rests on abduction from the observed data.
examples.cn: 该理论依靠从观察数据出发的溯因推理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱不打开」——有人把孩子抱起就走，爱他的人却打不开那扇车门。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ ducere（引导），构成 abducere（带走）；核心义是「把人或肢体从原处带离」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from criminal taking, through anatomical movement, to logical inference and popular culture.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从犯罪的带走，经过解剖学动作，走到逻辑推断与流行文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand leading someone away from where they belong
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把某人从其应在之处带走

branches.en: Criminal removal: a child or adult is taken against the law.
branches.cn: 犯罪的带离：儿童或成人被非法带走。

branches.en: Anatomical removal: a limb or muscle moves away from the midline.
branches.cn: 解剖学的带离：肢体或肌肉离开中线。

branches.en: Mental removal: the mind is led from a fact to a hidden cause.
branches.cn: 思维的带离：思维从事实被引向隐藏的原因。

branches.en: Animal removal: a cub is carried off from its group.
branches.cn: 动物的带离：幼崽被从群体中带走。

branches.en: Fictional removal: aliens carry a person away.
branches.cn: 虚构的带离：外星人把人带走。

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin prefix ab-, the verb stem duc-, and the noun ending -tion, with agent and patient endings in the family.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁前缀 ab-、动词词干 duc- 与名词后缀 -tion 构成，词族中还有施动者与受动者后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere is the shared source of a very large family, so the Latin entries show the verb and its noun rather than a single borrowed form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ducere 是一个庞大词族的共同来源，因此拉丁条目给出动词及其名词，而不是单一借词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「诱拐；绑架；使外展」
名词，义为「诱拐者；外展肌」
名词，义为「被绑架者」

definition_zh: 可恶的；令人憎恶的；令人反感的；与……相抵触的
definition_en: so hateful or disgusting that one recoils from it, or completely opposed to a principle
core_image: 人看到脏东西时本能地向后退、浑身起鸡皮疙瘩
scene: 档案里记录着看守如何虐待囚犯，读到的人都皱起眉头。Most readers find the guards' behaviour abhorrent.
sceneCN: 这里 abhorrent 是「令人憎恶的」（第 3 个义项：行为令人强烈反感）；句意为多数读者认为看守的行为令人憎恶。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「憎恶；厌恶」
由本词去掉形容词后缀构成，义为「憎恶；厌恶」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「令人憎恶地」

senses.title: Morally hateful
senses.definition: arousing strong moral disgust and condemnation
senses.definitionCN: 激起强烈的道德厌恶与谴责
senses.example: The exploitation of children is abhorrent.
senses.exampleCN: 剥削儿童是令人憎恶的。
senses.why: Latin abhorrere meant 'to shrink back bristling'; a moral horror repeats the body's instinctive recoil from something unclean.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abhorrere 意为「汗毛竖起地向后退」；道德上的憎恶，重复的正是身体对不洁之物的本能退缩。

senses.title: Revolting to the senses
senses.definition: so foul to smell, taste, or touch that one wants to pull away
senses.definitionCN: 在气味、味道或触感上极其污浊，让人想抽身避开
senses.example: The smell from the drain was abhorrent.
senses.exampleCN: 排水沟里传来的气味令人作呕。
senses.why: The root horrere is about bristling hair, so a stench that makes the skin crawl is the word's most physical use.
senses.whyCN: 词根 horrere 本指毛发竖起，因此让人起鸡皮疙瘩的恶臭是这个词最物理化的用法。

senses.title: Behaviour that disgusts
senses.definition: conduct that viewers or readers find deeply unacceptable
senses.definitionCN: 让旁观者或读者深感无法接受的行为
senses.example: Bullying is abhorrent to most students.
senses.exampleCN: 对多数学生来说，霸凌行为令人反感。
senses.why: Conduct can make observers recoil just as a sight or smell does; the moral audience repeats the physical gesture.
senses.whyCN: 行为也能让旁观者像看到景象或闻到气味那样退缩；道德上的旁观重复了这个身体动作。

senses.title: A crime that shocks
senses.definition: describing an offence whose cruelty causes public horror
senses.definitionCN: 形容残忍程度引发公众恐惧与厌恶的罪行
senses.example: The court condemned the abhorrent crime.
senses.exampleCN: 法院谴责了这起令人发指的罪行。
senses.why: Extreme wrongdoing is pictured as something so foul that the whole community steps back from it.
senses.whyCN: 极端的恶行被想象成极其污浊之物，整个社群都要从它面前退开。

senses.title: Opposed to a principle
senses.definition: completely inconsistent with a rule, value, or principle
senses.definitionCN: 与某项规则、价值或原则完全不一致
senses.example: Such treatment is abhorrent to the principles of the charter.
senses.exampleCN: 这种待遇与宪章的原则相抵触。
senses.why: The 'shrinking back' image turns abstract: a practice and a principle cannot stand together, so the mind recoils from the pairing.
senses.whyCN: 「向后退」的意象转向抽象：一种做法与一项原则无法并存，思维便从这个组合前退开。

senses.title: Contrary to reason
senses.definition: so unreasonable that it cannot be accepted by an ordinary mind
senses.definitionCN: 极度不合情理，普通人的理智无法接受
senses.example: It is abhorrent to reason to punish the victim.
senses.exampleCN: 惩罚受害者与常理不相容。
senses.why: Reason itself is treated as a standard a person can recoil from violating.
senses.whyCN: 理智本身被当作一条标准，人一旦违背它就会本能地退缩。

senses.title: An unacceptable system
senses.definition: describing an institution or practice that a society rejects as unjust
senses.definitionCN: 形容被社会视为不义而拒绝接受的制度或做法
senses.example: The old segregation laws were abhorrent.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的种族隔离法律令人无法接受。
senses.why: Institutions are judged by the same gut reaction once reserved for foul sights and smells.
senses.whyCN: 人们用曾经只针对污浊景象与气味的本能反应，来评判制度。

senses.title: An attitude one rejects
senses.definition: describing a view or attitude that decent people refuse to hold
senses.definitionCN: 形容正派人不愿持有的观点或态度
senses.example: She called the remarks abhorrent and demanded an apology.
senses.exampleCN: 她称这些言论令人憎恶，并要求道歉。
senses.why: Words and attitudes can also carry contamination; the listener pulls back as if from something dirty.
senses.whyCN: 言辞与态度也会带着污浊；听者像避开脏东西一样向后退。

intro.en: Abhorrent comes from a Latin verb for shrinking back with bristling hair, which also gave English horror.
intro.cn: abhorrent 来自一个表示「汗毛竖起、向后退」的拉丁语动词，英语 horror 也由它而来。

items.en: The root *ghers- is reconstructed with the sense 'to bristle'; the link to Latin horrere is generally accepted but not certain in every detail.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *ghers- 被重构为「毛发竖起」之义；它与拉丁语 horrere 的联系一般被接受，但细节并非全部确定。

items.en: horrere meant 'to bristle, tremble, shudder', and it is the source of horror.
items.cn: horrere 意为「毛发竖起、发抖、战栗」，是 horror 的来源。

items.en: ab- 'away' plus horrere formed abhorrere, 'to shrink back from with horror'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 horrere 构成 abhorrere，意为「因恐惧而向后退避」。

items.en: The present participle abhorrens, 'shrinking back from', is the direct model of the English adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 abhorrens 意为「对……退缩的」，是英语形容词的直接模型。

items.en: English formed abhorrent from the Latin participle, first in the sense of physical recoil.
items.cn: 英语由这个拉丁语分词构成 abhorrent，最初表示身体上的退缩。

items.en: The moral sense broadened until anything hateful, and later anything inconsistent with a principle, could be called abhorrent.
items.cn: 道德义不断扩展，直到任何可恨之事、后来任何与原则不符之事，都可以被称为 abhorrent。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, the noun, and the adverb from the same family; the second gathers adjectives of strong dislike.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的动词、名词与副词；第二组收表示强烈厌恶的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning intense disgust and hatred.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「憎恶、厌恶」，指强烈的反感与痛恨。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to hate something deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「憎恶、痛恨」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in a hateful or disgusting way'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「令人憎恶地」。

entries.definition: The noun for a feeling of fear and revulsion, from the same bristling root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恐惧、惊恐」，与 abhorrent 共享表示毛发竖起的词根。

entries.definition: Extremely distasteful or unacceptable, often to a moral sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人反感的」，常指道德上难以接受。

entries.definition: Deserving strong dislike; thoroughly hateful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可憎的」，指理应受到强烈厌恶。

entries.definition: Causing disgust, especially something foul or diseased.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人作呕的」，尤指污浊或病态之物。

entries.definition: Deserving contempt because of low or cruel behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「卑鄙的、可鄙的」，因行为卑劣残忍而应受蔑视。

entries.definition: Extremely unpleasant and causing a strong physical reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人作呕的」，指极度不快并引发强烈生理反应。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin root shared with horror and the fixed 'abhorrent to' pattern; the abstract hooks picture the recoil itself.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用与 horror 共享的拉丁词根和固定的 abhorrent to 结构；抽象记忆点想象退缩的动作。

normal.en: Abhorrent and horror share the Latin root for bristling hair; horror is the feeling, abhorrent is what causes it.
normal.cn: abhorrent 与 horror 共享表示毛发竖起的拉丁词根；horror 是感受，abhorrent 是引起感受的东西。

normal.en: Abhorrent to is the fixed pattern for something inconsistent with a principle.
normal.cn: abhorrent to 是固定结构，表示与某项原则不相容。

normal.en: Abhor is the verb, abhorrence the noun, abhorrent the adjective.
normal.cn: 动词是 abhor，名词是 abhorrence，形容词是 abhorrent。

normal.en: Morally abhorrent is a frequent pairing in news and commentary.
normal.cn: morally abhorrent 是新闻与评论中的高频搭配。

normal.en: The -ent ending marks a present participle, so abhorrent is literally 'shrinking back'.
normal.cn: -ent 结尾标明现在分词，所以 abhorrent 字面就是「正在退缩的」。

abstract.en: Picture a person stepping back and covering the nose at a filthy smell.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人闻到污浊气味，后退一步并捂住鼻子。

abstract.en: Picture hair standing up on the back of a neck in sudden disgust.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵突来的厌恶让后颈的汗毛竖起。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd turning away from a cruel act as if from a bad smell.
abstract.cn: 想象人群像避开恶臭一样，从残忍行为前转过身去。

examples.en: Racism is abhorrent to any fair society.
examples.cn: 种族主义与任何公平社会都格格不入。

examples.en: The idea of selling the school was abhorrent to parents.
examples.cn: 卖掉这所学校的想法让家长们无法接受。

examples.en: He found the cruelty of the experiment abhorrent.
examples.cn: 他觉得这项实验的残忍令人憎恶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿伯恨他」——阿伯一看见那人做的事就浑身发冷、连连后退，恨得不愿靠近。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ horrere（毛发竖起、发抖），构成 abhorrere（因恐惧而退缩）；核心义是「一见就起鸡皮疙瘩地退开」

sensesIntro.en: The senses begin with physical revulsion and moral disgust, then extend to behaviour, crime, institutions, and ideas that conflict with principle.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从生理上的作呕与道德厌恶开始，再扩展到行为、罪行、制度，以及与原则冲突的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body stepping back with hair standing on end
core.cn: 核心意象：汗毛竖起、身体向后退的一步

branches.en: Physical and moral disgust: the body and the conscience both recoil.
branches.cn: 生理与道德的厌恶：身体与良知同时退缩。

branches.en: People and their words become revolting to the audience.
branches.cn: 人及其言辞让受众产生强烈反感。

branches.en: Crimes and institutions are condemned as foul and unacceptable.
branches.cn: 罪行与制度被谴责为污浊、不可接受。

branches.en: The recoil turns abstract: a practice conflicts with a principle or with reason.
branches.cn: 退缩转向抽象：做法与原则或理智发生冲突。

branches.en: The fixed phrase abhorrent to marks that conflict grammatically.
branches.cn: 固定短语 abhorrent to 在语法上标出这种冲突。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem hor r-, the prefix ab-, and the adjective and noun endings -ent, -ence, and -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 horr-、前缀 ab-，以及形容词与名词后缀 -ent、-ence、-ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin horrere is the shared source of horror, horrid, and abhorrent, so the Latin entries record the verb and its participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 horrere 是 horror、horrid 与 abhorrent 的共同来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其分词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「憎恶；厌恶」
动词，义为「憎恶；厌恶」

definition_zh: 遵守；容忍；持续；居住；停留；承受
definition_en: to accept or obey a rule, to tolerate something, or to remain in a place or state
core_image: 一个人站在原地不动，时间从身边流过
scene: 她把那枚旧罗盘挂在墙上，说它陪自己走过每一段航程。The memory of that summer abided with her for years.
sceneCN: 这里 abide 是「持续存在、留在心中」（第 3 个义项：某事物长期存续）；句意为那个夏天的记忆在她心中留存多年。

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转为形容词，义为「持久的；不变的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「遵守；居住」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「遵守者；居住者」

senses.title: To obey a rule
senses.definition: to accept and act according to a rule, law, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 接受并按照规则、法律或协议行事
senses.example: All members must abide by the club's rules.
senses.exampleCN: 所有成员都必须遵守俱乐部的规则。
senses.why: Old English abidan meant 'to remain'; to abide by a rule is to remain inside its boundary instead of leaving it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 abidan 意为「停留」；abide by a rule 就是留在规则的边界之内，不越出去。

senses.title: To tolerate something
senses.definition: to put up with a person or thing one dislikes
senses.definitionCN: 忍受自己不喜欢的人或事物
senses.example: She cannot abide people who talk during films.
senses.exampleCN: 她无法容忍看电影时说话的人。
senses.why: Tolerating something is staying in its presence without walking away, so 'remain' turns into 'endure'.
senses.whyCN: 容忍就是在它面前待着而不走开，于是「停留」变成了「忍受」。

senses.title: To continue to exist
senses.definition: of a feeling, memory, or condition, to last
senses.definitionCN: 指情感、记忆或状况长期存续
senses.example: The old custom still abides in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老习俗仍在村中延续。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to remain; what remains over time is what continues to exist.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「停留」；随时间留下来的东西，就是继续存在的东西。

senses.title: To dwell somewhere
senses.definition: to live or stay in a place, now mainly literary or archaic
senses.definitionCN: 住在某地，现多用于文学或古语
senses.example: He abode in a small cottage by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他住在海边的一间小屋。
senses.why: A person who remains in one place is, in the old sense, dwelling there; the past form abode became a noun for a home.
senses.whyCN: 留在某地的人，按古老含义就是住在那里；过去式 abode 后来变成了表示「住所」的名词。

senses.title: To wait for something
senses.definition: to wait for a time or event, especially in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 等待某个时刻或事件，尤见于较早的用法
senses.example: We must abide the right moment to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须等待合适的发言时机。
senses.why: To remain in place until something happens is to wait for it; the waiting sense survives in older and literary English.
senses.whyCN: 在原地留到某事发生，就是等待；这个「等待」义保留在较早和文学化的英语里。

senses.title: To endure consequences
senses.definition: to accept and suffer the results of an action
senses.definitionCN: 接受并承担某一行为的后果
senses.example: Those who break the law must abide the consequences.
senses.exampleCN: 违法者必须承受后果。
senses.why: Enduring a result is remaining under its weight without fleeing; the same 'stay' image becomes moral stamina.
senses.whyCN: 承受结果就是在它的重压下留下而不逃开；同一个「停留」意象变成了道德上的坚韧。

senses.title: To remain faithful
senses.definition: to stay loyal to a faith, promise, or person
senses.definitionCN: 对信仰、承诺或某人保持忠诚
senses.example: They abode in their faith through years of hardship.
senses.exampleCN: 多年困苦中，他们坚守着自己的信仰。
senses.why: Faith is a place one stays in; abiding is refusing to move out even when conditions are hard.
senses.whyCN: 信仰是一个人停留的地方；坚守就是即使艰难也不搬离。

senses.title: To linger in a place
senses.definition: to stay in a place for a time rather than leave immediately
senses.definitionCN: 在某地待上一段时间，而不是立刻离开
senses.example: The scent of pine abided in the empty room.
senses.exampleCN: 松木的气味留在空房间里。
senses.why: The concrete 'remain in place' sense applies to scents and presences that outlast their source.
senses.whyCN: 具体的「留在原处」义，适用于那些比来源留存更久的味道与气息。

intro.en: Abide is a native Germanic word meaning 'to remain', and most of its senses are extensions of staying in place.
intro.cn: abide 是一个本土日耳曼词，意为「停留」，它的大多数义项都是「留在原处」的延伸。

items.en: The root *bheidh- is reconstructed with the sense 'to wait, trust'; the reconstruction is standard but the semantic path is uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *bheidh- 被重构为「等待、信任」之义；这一重构是通行的，但语义演变路径不确定。

items.en: The Germanic verb *bidan meant 'to wait, remain', and it also produced the modern verb bide.
items.cn: 日耳曼语动词 *bidan 意为「等待、停留」，现代动词 bide 也由它而来。

items.en: Old English abidan combined a- 'on' with bidan 'to wait', giving 'to remain, wait for'.
items.cn: 古英语 abidan 由 a-（在……上）与 bidan（等待）组合，意为「停留、等待」。

items.en: The past form abode also became a noun meaning 'a dwelling, a home'.
items.cn: 过去式 abode 同时演变为名词，义为「住所、家」。

items.en: The 'remain' sense survives chiefly in literary use, while 'abide by' became the everyday legal and moral phrase.
items.cn: 「停留」义主要保留在文学用法里，而 abide by 成为日常的法律与道德短语。

items.en: The negative 'cannot abide' developed from 'cannot remain with' into 'cannot tolerate'.
items.cn: 否定的 cannot abide 从「无法与之共处」发展出「无法容忍」的意思。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective, noun, and related native verbs; the second gathers verbs of obeying, tolerating, and remaining.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词、名词与相关的本土动词；第二组收表示遵守、容忍与停留的动词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning lasting or enduring, as in an abiding interest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「持久的、不变的」，如 an abiding interest（持久的兴趣）。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of obeying or remaining.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遵守；居住」，指遵守或停留的行为。

entries.definition: A home or dwelling; it began as the past tense of abide.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住所、家」，原先是 abide 的过去式。

entries.definition: To wait or remain, as in bide one's time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「等待、停留」，如 bide one's time（等待时机）。

entries.definition: To carry out the orders or rules of another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「服从、遵守」，执行他人的命令或规则。

entries.definition: To allow something one dislikes to continue without protest.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容忍」，不加反对地允许不喜欢的事物继续。

entries.definition: To suffer something difficult patiently over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受」，长时间耐心地承受艰难。

entries.definition: To stay in the same place or state.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「保持、停留」，留在同一地点或状态。

entries.definition: To live in a place, or to keep thinking about something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「居住」，也指持续思考某事。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the two everyday patterns 'abide by' and 'cannot abide', plus the family of forms; the abstract hooks picture staying in place.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用两个日常结构 abide by 与 cannot abide，加上词族形式；抽象记忆点想象留在原地。

normal.en: Abide by the rules is the common legal and moral pattern for obeying.
normal.cn: abide by the rules 是表示遵守的常见法律与道德结构。

normal.en: Cannot abide means cannot tolerate, as in 'I cannot abide that noise'.
normal.cn: cannot abide 意为无法容忍，如「我受不了那噪音」。

normal.en: Law-abiding citizens keep the law; the -ing form works inside a compound.
normal.cn: law-abiding citizens 指守法的公民；-ing 形式可用于复合词中。

normal.en: The past tense abode is also the noun for a home.
normal.cn: 过去式 abode 同时也是表示「住所」的名词。

normal.en: Bide and abide share the old Germanic verb for waiting.
normal.cn: bide 与 abide 共享古老的日耳曼语「等待」动词。

abstract.en: Picture a marker stone that never moves while seasons pass around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块界石始终不动，四季从它身边流过。

abstract.en: Picture a man standing under a rule painted on a wall, never stepping past the line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在墙上写着的规则之下，从不越过那条线。

abstract.en: Picture a smell that stays in a room long after the flowers are gone.
abstract.cn: 想象花香早已不在，气味却仍留在房间里。

examples.en: Everyone must abide by the safety rules.
examples.cn: 每个人都必须遵守安全规则。

examples.en: I cannot abide his constant complaining.
examples.cn: 我无法忍受他没完没了的抱怨。

examples.en: The custom has abided for centuries.
examples.cn: 这个习俗已经延续了几个世纪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额拜德」——像一枚钉子钉在原地，人守在那里不走，规则也就守住了。

root: 古英语 a-（在……上）+ bidan（等待、停留），源自古日耳曼语 *bidan；核心义是「留在原地不动」

sensesIntro.en: The senses all grow from 'remain in place': staying inside a rule, staying beside what one dislikes, staying over time, and staying in a home or a faith.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都从「留在原地」生长出来：留在规则之内、留在不喜欢的事物旁边、随时间留存，以及留在住所或信仰里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing still while time moves past
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身影站着不动，时间从旁流过

branches.en: Staying inside a boundary: rules, promises, and faith are kept.
branches.cn: 留在边界之内：规则、承诺与信仰得到遵守。

branches.en: Staying under pressure: what one dislikes or suffers is endured.
branches.cn: 留在压力之下：不喜欢或艰难的事物被忍受。

branches.en: Staying over time: customs, memories, and scents persist.
branches.cn: 随时间留下：习俗、记忆与气味持续存在。

branches.en: Staying in one place: the old dwelling sense, now mainly literary.
branches.cn: 留在某地：古老的居住义，现主要用于文学。

branches.en: Staying until an event comes: the old waiting sense.
branches.cn: 留到事件来临：古老的等待义。

intro.en: The word is a native Germanic formation, so the useful pieces are the prefix a-, the stem bid-, and the endings that build the family.
intro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语构成，因此有用的构件是前缀 a-、词干 bid-，以及构成词族的后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for abide; the closest Latin-family entries are words for waiting and remaining, offered only as semantic parallels.
latinIntro.cn: abide 没有拉丁语祖先；最接近的拉丁条目是表示等待与停留的词，仅作为语义参照。

scene: 赛后教练指着记分板，说这孩子天生就该做这件事。Her ability to read the game impressed every coach in the league.
sceneCN: 这里 ability 是「才能、天赋」（第 2 个义项：自然具备的出众本领）；句意为她解读比赛的能力让联盟里每位教练都印象深刻。

senses.title: Capacity to do something
senses.definition: the general power to perform an action or achieve a result
senses.definitionCN: 完成某个动作或取得某种结果的一般能力
senses.example: She has the ability to solve complex problems.
senses.exampleCN: 她有解决复杂问题的能力。
senses.why: Latin habilitas meant 'aptness', from habilis 'easy to handle'; the core is a hand that can take hold of a task.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 habilitas 意为「适宜、灵巧」，来自 habilis（好用的、拿得住的）；核心是一双能握住任务的手。

senses.title: Natural talent
senses.definition: an inborn capacity that makes someone unusually good at something
senses.definitionCN: 使人某方面格外出色的先天能力
senses.example: His ability at the piano was obvious by age five.
senses.exampleCN: 他五岁时钢琴天赋就已显露。
senses.why: The inborn version of ability is a hand that already fits the tool before any training; the Latin idea of aptness covered both nature and practice.
senses.whyCN: 天赋版本的能力，是尚未训练就已合手的那只手；拉丁语「灵巧」的观念同时涵盖天性（nature）与练习。

senses.title: A learned skill
senses.definition: a competence developed through practice and training
senses.definitionCN: 通过练习与训练发展出来的熟练本领
senses.example: The course builds the ability to write clear reports.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程培养撰写清晰报告的能力。
senses.why: Practice turns the general power into a reliable grip, so the same hand image moves from potential to trained use.
senses.whyCN: 练习把一般的力量变成可靠的握力，于是同一个手的意象从潜能走向训练有素的运用。

senses.title: Legal or financial capacity
senses.definition: the legal right or financial means to do something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的法定权利或经济手段
senses.example: The court assessed the company's ability to pay.
senses.exampleCN: 法院评估了该公司的支付能力。
senses.why: Law and finance measure capacity as the power to act or to carry a burden, so able becomes a matter of right and means.
senses.whyCN: 法律与财务把能力衡量为行动的力量或承担负担的力量，于是 able 变成权利与财力的问题。

senses.title: Mental capacity
senses.definition: the power of the mind to understand, reason, and remember
senses.definitionCN: 理解、推理与记忆的心智能力
senses.example: The test measures verbal ability in children.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试测量儿童的语言能力。
senses.why: The mind is treated as a hand that grasps ideas; understanding and memory are ways of holding them.
senses.whyCN: 心智被当作握住观念的手；理解与记忆就是握住它们的方式。

senses.title: Physical capacity
senses.definition: the body's power to move, endure, or perform
senses.definitionCN: 身体活动、耐受或完成动作的力量
senses.example: Regular training improved her physical ability.
senses.exampleCN: 规律训练提升了她的体能。
senses.why: The body is the original tool, so physical ability is simply the strength to move and to endure.
senses.whyCN: 身体是最原始的工具，因此体能与力量就是移动与耐受的本钱。

senses.title: Proven performance
senses.definition: a level of competence shown in real tasks rather than claimed
senses.definitionCN: 在真实任务中表现出来的水平，而非口头声称
senses.example: Promotion depends on demonstrated ability.
senses.exampleCN: 晋升取决于已展现的能力。
senses.why: What has been proven is what the hand has actually held; demonstrated ability is the record of successful grips.
senses.whyCN: 被证明的能力，是手真正握住过的东西；demonstrated ability 就是成功握持的记录。

senses.title: Inherent power of a thing
senses.definition: the capacity of an object or system to produce an effect
senses.definitionCN: 物体或系统产生某种效果的性能
senses.example: The ability of the material to resist heat was tested.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料的耐热性能接受了测试。
senses.why: A material or system can also hold a force or perform a task, so ability extends to what an object can withstand or do.
senses.whyCN: 材料或系统也能承受力量或完成任务，因此 ability 扩展到物体能承受或能做到什么。

intro.en: Ability comes from a Latin word for being handy or apt, built on the verb 'to hold'.
intro.cn: ability 来自一个表示「灵巧、适宜」的拉丁词，其基础是「握持」这个动词。

items.en: The root *ghebh- is reconstructed with the sense 'to take, hold'; the details of the reconstruction are debated.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *ghebh- 被重构为「拿、握」之义；重构的具体细节仍有争论。

items.en: habere meant 'to have, hold', and it produced habit, exhibit, and prohibit.
items.cn: habere 意为「拥有、握持」，衍生出 habit、exhibit、prohibit 等词。

items.en: habilis meant 'easy to hold or handle, apt, handy', a word used of tools as well as people.
items.cn: habilis 意为「好拿好用的、灵巧的」，既可形容工具，也可形容人。

items.en: habilitas named the quality of being apt, the direct ancestor of the English noun.
items.cn: habilitas 指「灵巧、适宜」的性质，是英语名词的直接祖先。

items.en: Old French ablete carried the sense 'aptitude, cleverness' into medieval use.
items.cn: 古法语 ablete 把「才干、机敏」之义带入中世纪用法。

items.en: English ability broadened from personal aptitude to legal capacity and to the performance of objects.
items.cn: 英语 ability 从个人资质扩展到法律资格，再扩展到物体的性能。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective, adverb, and negative forms built on the same stem; the second gathers words for competence.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干构成的形容词、副词与否定形式；第二组收表示胜任的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning having the power or skill to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有能力的」，指具备做事的力量或技能。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a competent or skillful way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「能干地、巧妙地」。

entries.definition: The noun meaning lack of ability or power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无能力、无法」，指缺少能力或力量。

entries.definition: A condition that limits a person's physical or mental activity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「残疾」，指限制身体或心智活动的状况。

entries.definition: The power or potential to do something, often of a system or person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能力、潜能」，常指系统或人具备的力量。

entries.definition: The ability to do a task to an acceptable standard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胜任、能力」，指达到可接受标准地完成任务的本领。

entries.definition: A learned ability to do something well, especially with the hands or mind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「技能」，指通过练习获得的熟练本领。

entries.definition: A natural ability that may develop into high achievement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天赋」，指可能发展为卓越成就的先天能力。

entries.definition: A natural readiness to learn or do a particular kind of work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「资质、天资」，指学习或从事某类工作的先天倾向。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks work from the Latin verb for holding and the common 'ability to' pattern; the abstract hooks picture the hand that can reach and hold.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点来自表示「握持」的拉丁动词与常见的 ability to 结构；抽象记忆点想象够得着、握得住的手。

normal.en: Ability and able share Latin habilis, which described something easy to hold or handle.
normal.cn: ability 与 able 共享拉丁语 habilis，后者形容好拿、好用的东西。

normal.en: The ability to do something is the standard pattern, often followed by a verb.
normal.cn: the ability to do something 是标准结构，后面常接动词。

normal.en: Natural ability is inborn; demonstrated ability is proven in real tasks.
normal.cn: natural ability 是先天具备的；demonstrated ability 是在真实任务中证明的。

normal.en: Ability to pay is a legal and financial phrase about money.
normal.cn: ability to pay 是关于金钱的法律与经济短语。

normal.en: Inability adds in-, and disability adds dis- to the same noun.
normal.cn: inability 加 in-，disability 加 dis-，都接在同一个名词上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand stretching up and closing around a tool just out of reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手向上伸展，正好握住原本够不着的工具。

abstract.en: Picture a pianist's fingers finding the keys without looking.
abstract.cn: 想象钢琴家的手指不看着琴键也能准确落位。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge bearing weight that engineers once thought impossible.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥承受住工程师曾认为不可能承受的重量。

examples.en: He has a remarkable ability to learn languages.
examples.cn: 他有一种非凡的语言学习能力。

examples.en: The job requires the ability to work under pressure.
examples.cn: 这份工作需要抗压能力。

examples.en: Her abilities were recognized early at school.
examples.cn: 她的才能在学校很早就得到认可。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿比勒提」——手一伸就够到高处，握得住工具，这就是有本事。

root: 拉丁语 habilitas（灵巧、适宜），源自 habilis（好用的、拿得住的），再往前是 habere（握持）；核心义是「握得住、做得到」

sensesIntro.en: The senses range from general capacity and inborn talent to learned, legal, mental, physical, demonstrated, and mechanical forms of capacity.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从一般能力与先天天赋，扩展到习得、法律、心智、身体、已展现以及物体性能等各种能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that can reach the tool and hold it firm
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手够得到工具并能握稳

branches.en: What a person can do by nature or in general.
branches.cn: 一个人天生能做或总体能做的事。

branches.en: Trained, mental, and bodily powers developed through practice.
branches.cn: 通过练习发展的技能、心智与身体力量。

branches.en: Legal and financial capacity recognized by institutions.
branches.cn: 制度所承认的法律与经济能力。

branches.en: Competence proven in real performance rather than claimed.
branches.cn: 在真实表现中证明的胜任力，而非口头声称。

branches.en: The inherent power of a material or system to produce an effect.
branches.cn: 材料或系统产生某种效果的内在性能。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem habilit-, the adjective ending -ity, and the privative prefixes in- and dis-.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 habilit-、名词后缀 -ity，以及否定前缀 in- 与 dis- 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere is the shared source of ability, habit, and prohibit, so the Latin entries show the verb and the derived nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere 是 ability、habit、prohibit 的共同来源，因此拉丁条目给出动词与派生名词。
