sceneCN: 这里 able 是「能够的」（第 1 个义项：具备做某事的力量或条件）；句意为他们能在天黑前抵达受困村民。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「能力；才能」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「能干地；巧妙地」
由使动前缀加本词构成，义为「使能够；启用」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「使丧失能力；禁用」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不能的；无能力的」

senses.title: Having the power to do something
senses.definition: having the physical or practical power to do something
senses.definitionCN: 具备完成某事的力量或现实条件
senses.example: The rescue team was able to reach the village.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队得以抵达那个村庄。
senses.why: Latin habilis meant 'easy to handle'; an able person is one who can take a task in hand and manage it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 habilis 意为「好拿好用的」；able 的人就是能把任务接在手里并处理妥当的人。

senses.title: Competent and skillful
senses.definition: showing a high level of skill in one's work
senses.definitionCN: 在工作中表现出很高的技能水平
senses.example: She is an able administrator.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位能干的行政主管。
senses.why: The same holding image becomes a judgement of quality: the person handles things well, not merely possibly.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「握持」意象转为质量评判：这个人把事情处理得好，而不只是「有可能做」。

senses.title: Physically fit
senses.definition: having a healthy body and normal physical function
senses.definitionCN: 身体健康、身体功能正常
senses.example: The job requires an able body.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作需要健全的体魄。
senses.why: In older use able referred to bodily fitness, especially for service or work.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的用法里，able 指身体适合服役或劳动。

senses.title: Legally qualified
senses.definition: having the legal right or standing to do something
senses.definitionCN: 拥有做某事的法定权利或资格
senses.example: He is able to sign the contract on the company's behalf.
senses.exampleCN: 他有权代表公司签署合同。
senses.why: Capacity before the law is pictured as the power to act, so able extends from the body to legal standing.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的能力被想象成行动的力量，于是 able 从身体延伸到法律地位。

senses.title: Capable of functioning
senses.definition: of a device or system, having the capacity to perform a function
senses.definitionCN: 指设备或系统具备执行某种功能的能力
senses.example: The sensor is able to detect very small movements.
senses.exampleCN: 这个传感器能够探测非常细微的动作。
senses.why: Tools are described with the same word as people: what can do its job is able.
senses.whyCN: 工具与人用同一个词来描述：能完成本职工作的东西就是 able。

senses.title: Suited to a role
senses.definition: having the qualities needed for a particular role or task
senses.definitionCN: 具备担任某个角色或完成某项任务所需的品质
senses.example: They chose the ablest candidate for the post.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这个职位挑选了最能胜任的人选。
senses.why: The superlative ablest marks the top of a scale of fitness for a role.
senses.whyCN: 最高级 ablest 标出胜任某一角色的最高水平。

senses.title: Resourceful
senses.definition: quick to find a way of dealing with a difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 能迅速找到应对困难的办法
senses.example: An able negotiator can unblock a deadlock.
senses.exampleCN: 有办法的谈判者能打破僵局。
senses.why: Resourcefulness is the practical face of ability: the hand finds something to hold even when the obvious tool is missing.
senses.whyCN: 机智是能力在实践中的面孔：即使手边没有现成工具，那只手也能找到可以握住的东西。

senses.title: Financially capable
senses.definition: having enough money to meet a cost or obligation
senses.definitionCN: 拥有足够的钱来支付费用或履行义务
senses.example: Only a few families are able to pay such fees.
senses.exampleCN: 只有少数家庭负担得起这样的费用。
senses.why: Ability in the economic sense is again the power to carry a weight, here measured in money.
senses.whyCN: 经济意义上的 ability 仍是承受重量的力量，只不过用金钱来衡量。

intro.en: Able came through French from a Latin adjective meaning handy or easy to handle, built on the verb for holding.
intro.cn: able 经由法语来自一个意为「好用、好把握」的拉丁形容词，其基础是表示「握持」的动词。

items.en: The root *ghebh- is reconstructed with the sense 'to take, hold'; details of the reconstruction remain debated.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *ghebh- 被重构为「拿、握」之义；重构细节仍有争论。

items.en: habere meant 'to have, hold' and lies behind habit and prohibit as well.
items.cn: habere 意为「拥有、握持」，habit 与 prohibit 也由它而来。

items.en: habilis meant 'easy to hold, handy, apt'; it described a well-balanced tool as readily as a skillful person.
items.cn: habilis 意为「好拿的、顺手的、灵巧的」，既能形容称手的工具，也能形容熟练的人。

items.en: Old French able or hable carried the adjective into medieval French with the sense 'fit, capable'.
items.cn: 古法语 able 或 hable 把这个形容词带入中世纪法语，意为「适合的、有能力的」。

items.en: English able is recorded from the fourteenth century, first in the sense of bodily fitness and legal capacity.
items.cn: 英语 able 自十四世纪有记录，最初表示身体适合与法律资格。

items.en: The be able to pattern made the word the ordinary way of expressing possibility and achievement.
items.cn: be able to 这一结构使这个词成为表达「可能」与「做到」的日常方式。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and prefixed verbs of the same family; the second gathers adjectives of competence.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的名词、副词与带前缀的动词；第二组收表示胜任的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning the power or skill to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能力、才能」，指做事的力量或技能。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a capable or skillful manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「能干地、巧妙地」。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make someone or something able to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使能够」，指使人或物具备做事的能力。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to take away the power to act or to switch off.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使丧失能力；禁用」，指剥夺行动能力或关闭功能。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning not having the power or opportunity to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不能的」，指没有能力或机会做某事。

entries.definition: Having the ability or qualities needed for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有能力的、能胜任的」，具备完成任务所需的能力或品质。

entries.definition: Adequately skilled for a particular job or standard.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「胜任的」，具备达到某项工作或标准所需的技能。

entries.definition: Trained and experienced in a particular activity.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「熟练的」，在某一活动上受过训练并有经验。

entries.definition: Highly competent at something, often a language or tool.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精通的」，在某事上高度熟练，常指语言或工具。

entries.definition: Having the official training or legal right for a role.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有资格的」，具备担任某角色的正式训练或法定权利。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks work from the everyday 'be able to' pattern and the 'able-bodied' compound; the abstract hooks picture a hand finding the right tool.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点来自日常结构 be able to 与复合词 able-bodied；抽象记忆点想象手找到合适的工具。

normal.en: Be able to is the standard way to express that someone can do something.
normal.cn: be able to 是表达「某人能够做某事」的标准说法。

normal.en: Able-bodied describes a person with a healthy, functioning body.
normal.cn: able-bodied 形容身体健全、功能正常的人。

normal.en: Ability is the noun and ably the adverb from the same family.
normal.cn: 同族中 ability 是名词，ably 是副词。

normal.en: Enable adds the idea of giving power; disable takes it away.
normal.cn: enable 加上「给予能力」的意思，disable 则把能力拿走。

normal.en: Able seaman is an old nautical rank, showing the word's use for fitness for duty.
normal.cn: able seaman 是古老的航海职级，显示这个词曾用于表示适合服役。

abstract.en: Picture a hand opening a toolbox and choosing exactly the right tool.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手打开工具箱，恰好挑中需要的工具。

abstract.en: Picture a sailor climbing the rigging with steady, confident limbs.
abstract.cn: 想象水手用稳健自信的四肢攀上缆索。

abstract.en: Picture a lock that opens at one touch because it was made to fit that key.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁一碰就开，因为它正是为那把钥匙而造。

examples.en: She was able to finish the race despite the injury.
examples.cn: 尽管受伤，她仍能完成比赛。

examples.en: He is an able and trusted adviser.
examples.cn: 他是一位能干且受信任的顾问。

examples.en: The system is able to process thousands of records a minute.
examples.cn: 该系统每分钟能处理数千条记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿波」——工具箱一打开，手一伸就拿到合适的工具，事情自然办得成。

root: 拉丁语 habilis（顺手好用的），源自 habere（握持），经古法语 able 进入英语；核心义是「拿得住、办得成」

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from the plain power to do something, through skill and physical fitness, to legal, mechanical, and financial capacity.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从朴素的行事能力，经过技能与体能，走到法律、机械与经济上的能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that finds the right tool and holds it
core.cn: 核心意象：一只找到合适工具并握稳的手

branches.en: The plain power to act, whether of a person or a device.
branches.cn: 朴素的行事能力，无论是人还是设备。

branches.en: Skill and fitness for a role, judged on a scale of competence.
branches.cn: 胜任角色的技能与适合度，按能力高低评判。

branches.en: Bodily fitness, especially in older uses such as able-bodied.
branches.cn: 身体健全，尤见于 able-bodied 等较早用法。

branches.en: Legal standing and official right to act.
branches.cn: 法律地位与采取行动的正式权利。

branches.en: Practical resourcefulness and financial capacity to carry a burden.
branches.cn: 实际上的机智，以及承担费用的经济能力。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem habil-, shortened in French to able, with the verb prefixes en- and dis- and the noun ending -ity.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 habil-（在法语中缩为 able）、动词前缀 en- 与 dis-，以及名词后缀 -ity 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin habilis and habere are the shared source of able, ability, and enable, so the Latin entries record the adjective and the verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habilis 与 habere 是 able、ability、enable 的共同来源，因此拉丁条目记录形容词与动词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「能力；才能」
动词，义为「使能够；启用」

definition_zh: 住所；家；居住；逗留；栖身之处
definition_en: a place where someone lives or stays, often used in literary or formal writing
core_image: 一盏灯下有人长期停留的那间屋子
scene: 老人把钥匙交给来看房的人，说这间屋子他住了六十年。The old man called the cottage his abode for sixty years.
sceneCN: 这里 abode 是「住所、家」（第 1 个义项：某人居住的地方，带文学色彩）；句意为老人把这间小屋称作自己住了六十年的住所。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词词尾构成，义为「居住；停留；遵守」
由动词加现在分词后缀构成，义为「持久的；不变的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「居住；遵守」

senses.title: A home
senses.definition: a person's home, especially in literary or formal use
senses.definitionCN: 某人的家，尤用于文学或正式语境
senses.example: He made his abode in a quiet valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一个安静的山谷里安了家。
senses.why: Old English abad meant 'a staying'; a place where one stays becomes the place one calls home.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 abad 意为「停留」；一个人停留的地方，就成了他称作家的地方。

senses.title: The act of dwelling
senses.definition: the state or act of living in a place
senses.definitionCN: 在某地生活的状态或行为
senses.example: Their abode in the mountains lasted through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山中的居住持续了整个冬天。
senses.why: The noun first named the staying itself, not the building; the state and the place grew from the same word.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词最初指「停留」本身，而非建筑；状态与地点都从同一个词生长出来。

senses.title: A permanent residence
senses.definition: an established home where a person normally lives
senses.definitionCN: 一个人通常居住的固定住所
senses.example: The form asks for details of your permanent abode.
senses.exampleCN: 表格要求填写你的永久住所信息。
senses.why: Official language uses the word for the fixed address a person can be reached at.
senses.whyCN: 官方语言用这个词指可以找到某人的固定地址。

senses.title: An animal's dwelling
senses.definition: the place where an animal lives or rests
senses.definitionCN: 动物生活或休息的地方
senses.example: The cave was the abode of a small bat colony.
senses.exampleCN: 这个洞穴是一小群蝙蝠的栖身处。
senses.why: The human home image extends to animals, whose shelters are also places of staying.
senses.whyCN: 人的家宅意象扩展到动物，动物的庇护所同样是停留之处。

senses.title: A heavenly dwelling
senses.definition: a dwelling of gods, spirits, or the dead in religious writing
senses.definitionCN: 宗教文本中神灵、鬼魂或亡者的居所
senses.example: The hymn describes heaven as the abode of peace.
senses.exampleCN: 这首赞美诗把天堂描述为安宁的居所。
senses.why: Religious language treats the afterlife as a place one enters and stays in, so the home word becomes sacred.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言把来世当作进入并停留的地方，于是「家」的词带上神圣色彩。

senses.title: Temporary lodging
senses.definition: a place where someone stays for a limited time
senses.definitionCN: 某人短时间停留的地方
senses.example: They found a modest abode near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站附近找到一处简朴的住处。
senses.why: The 'staying' sense allows the word to cover short stays as well as lifelong homes.
senses.whyCN: 「停留」义让这个词既能指终身之家，也能指短暂居留。

senses.title: A figurative dwelling
senses.definition: a place where a quality or thing is said to reside
senses.definitionCN: 某种性质或事物被说成栖居的地方
senses.example: The library is an abode of quiet learning.
senses.exampleCN: 这座图书馆是安静学问的居所。
senses.why: Abstract things are imagined as residents with a home, a common literary extension of the dwelling image.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事物被想象成有家的居住者，这是居住意象常见的文学延伸。

senses.title: An official residence
senses.definition: the address officially recorded as someone's residence
senses.definitionCN: 被正式登记为某人住处的地址
senses.example: The census records every abode in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查记录了该区的每一处住所。
senses.why: Administration needs a countable label for each dwelling, so abode becomes a unit in records.
senses.whyCN: 行政需要给每处居所一个可计数的标签，于是 abode 成为档案中的一个单位。

intro.en: Abode is a native English noun from the verb abide, and it first meant the act of staying rather than the building.
intro.cn: abode 是来自动词 abide 的本土英语名词，最初指「停留」这一行为，而不是建筑物。

items.en: The root *bheidh- is reconstructed with the sense 'to wait, trust'; the reconstruction is standard but the semantic path is uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *bheidh- 被重构为「等待、信任」之义；这一重构是通行的，但语义路径不确定。

items.en: The Germanic verb *bidan meant 'to wait, remain' and also produced bide.
items.cn: 日耳曼语动词 *bidan 意为「等待、停留」，也衍生出 bide。

items.en: abidan combined a- 'on' with bidan, giving 'to remain, wait for'.
items.cn: abidan 由 a-（在……上）与 bidan 组合，意为「停留、等待」。

items.en: The noun abad meant 'a staying, a delay'; it is the direct ancestor of abode.
items.cn: 名词 abad 意为「停留、耽搁」，是 abode 的直接祖先。

items.en: The form abood appears in Middle English with the sense 'dwelling, home'.
items.cn: 形式 abood 在中古英语中出现，意为「住所、家」。

items.en: Modern English keeps abode mainly in literary, legal, and humorous phrases such as humble abode.
items.cn: 现代英语主要把 abode 保留在文学、法律与幽默短语中，如 humble abode。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb and related forms from which abode comes; the second gathers words for a place where someone lives.
note.cn: 第一组收 abode 所来自的动词与相关形式；第二组收表示人居住之处的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to remain, dwell, or obey.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「停留、居住」或「遵守」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning lasting or enduring.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「持久的、不变的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of remaining or obeying.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「居住」或「遵守」。

entries.definition: To wait or remain, as in bide one's time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「等待、停留」，如 bide one's time。

entries.definition: A house or place where a person lives, often in formal or legal use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住宅、居所」，常用于正式或法律语境。

entries.definition: The official or formal word for a person's home.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住所、居所」，是人居住之处的正式说法。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the place where one lives and belongs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「家」，是日常表示居住与归属之地的词。

entries.definition: A temporary place to stay, often rented.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「寄宿处、临时住处」，常指租住的地方。

entries.definition: The natural home of an animal or plant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「栖息地」，指动植物自然的家。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the legal phrases and the family link to abide; the abstract hooks picture a lit room where someone stays.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用法律短语以及与 abide 的词族联系；抽象记忆点想象一间亮着灯、有人停留的屋子。

normal.en: Place of abode and right of abode are standard legal phrases.
normal.cn: place of abode 与 right of abode 是标准法律短语。

normal.en: No fixed abode is the official phrase for someone without a permanent address.
normal.cn: no fixed abode 是官方说法，指没有固定住所的人。

normal.en: Humble abode is a polite, often humorous way to mention one's home.
normal.cn: humble abode 是提及自家时礼貌、常带幽默的说法。

normal.en: Abode comes from abide, the verb for staying, so the noun is literally 'a staying'.
normal.cn: abode 来自表示停留的动词 abide，因此这个名词字面就是「停留」。

normal.en: The plural abodes is regular and rare in speech but common in records.
normal.cn: 复数 abodes 变化规则，口语中少见，档案中常见。

abstract.en: Picture one lit window in a dark valley, with a chair that has been used for years.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗山谷中唯一亮着的窗，里面有一把用了多年的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a door key worn smooth by decades of turning.
abstract.cn: 想象一把被几十年转动磨得光滑的门钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a cave where bats hang in rows, a quiet animal home.
abstract.cn: 想象洞穴里蝙蝠成排倒挂，那是一处安静的动物之家。

examples.en: They took up their abode near the river.
examples.cn: 他们在河边安了家。

examples.en: The suspect has no fixed abode.
examples.cn: 嫌疑人没有固定住所。

examples.en: The temple was regarded as the abode of the gods.
examples.cn: 这座神庙被视为众神的居所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额波德」——一盏灯、一把旧椅子，人在那儿一住多年，那间屋子就是住所。

root: 古英语 abad（停留），来自 abidan（停留、等待），再往前是日耳曼语 *bidan；核心义是「长期停留之处」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the act of staying to a home, then to permanent, animal, heavenly, temporary, figurative, and official dwellings.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从「停留」的行为走到家，再扩展到永久、动物、天上、临时、比喻与官方登记的居所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room where someone has long stayed
core.cn: 核心意象：有人长久停留的一间亮灯屋子

branches.en: A person's home, whether described by a writer or recorded by an office.
branches.cn: 人的家，或由作家描写，或由机构登记。

branches.en: The act or period of staying, including temporary lodging.
branches.cn: 停留的行为或时段，包括临时住处。

branches.en: An animal's shelter, where a creature makes its home.
branches.cn: 动物的庇护所，生物在那里安家。

branches.en: A sacred dwelling for gods or spirits.
branches.cn: 神灵或鬼魂的神圣居所。

branches.en: A figurative home for a quality such as learning or peace.
branches.cn: 学问或安宁等性质的比喻性居所。

intro.en: Abode is a native Germanic noun, so the useful pieces are the stem bod- and the endings that build the family from abide.
intro.cn: abode 是本土日耳曼语名词，因此有用的构件是词干 bod-，以及从 abide 构成词族的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Abode has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries are left empty rather than inventing a borrowed form.
latinIntro.cn: abode 没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁条目留空，而不编造借词形式。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「居住；停留；遵守」
形容词，义为「持久的；不变的」

definition_zh: 废除；废止；取消；消灭
definition_en: to end a law, system, practice, or institution officially and completely
core_image: 一块写着旧规矩的木牌被当众摘下、劈碎
scene: 议会大厅里，人们举手通过一项终结旧制度的议案。Parliament voted to abolish the outdated law.
sceneCN: 这里 abolish 是「废除」（第 1 个义项：正式终止一项法律）；句意为议会投票废除了那项过时的法律。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「废除；废止」
由名词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「废奴主义者；主张废除者」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「废除者」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「可废除的」

senses.title: To repeal a law
senses.definition: to end a law officially so that it no longer has force
senses.definitionCN: 正式终止一项法律，使其不再有效
senses.example: Parliament voted to abolish the outdated law.
senses.exampleCN: 议会投票废除了那项过时的法律。
senses.why: Latin abolere meant 'to destroy, wipe out'; a law is wiped from the statute book as a mark is wiped from a surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abolere 意为「摧毁、抹去」；法律被从法令全书中抹掉，就像记号从表面被擦去。

senses.title: To end a system
senses.definition: to put an end to an established system or structure
senses.definitionCN: 终止一套已确立的制度或结构
senses.example: The reform abolished the old examination system.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革废止了旧的考试制度。
senses.why: A system is a standing structure; abolishing it removes the structure itself, not merely one of its rules.
senses.whyCN: 制度是一种长期矗立的结构；废除它是拆掉结构本身，而不只是其中一条规则。

senses.title: To end a custom
senses.definition: to stop a long-standing social custom from being practised
senses.definitionCN: 使一种长期存在的社会习俗不再被实行
senses.example: The village abolished the custom of paying dowries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄取消了支付嫁妆的习俗。
senses.why: Customs are treated like laws written in the community's memory, and abolishing them erases that entry.
senses.whyCN: 习俗被当作写在社群记忆里的法律，废除它就是擦掉那一条。

senses.title: To discontinue a practice
senses.definition: to stop using a method or practice completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底停止使用某种方法或做法
senses.example: The company abolished the daily report.
senses.exampleCN: 公司取消了每日汇报的做法。
senses.why: A practice can be removed as an object is removed from a room, leaving the space empty.
senses.whyCN: 一种做法可以像物品被搬出房间那样被移除，只留下空位。

senses.title: To eliminate a social ill
senses.definition: to eradicate a harmful condition such as poverty or illiteracy
senses.definitionCN: 根除贫困、文盲等有害状况
senses.example: The campaign aimed to abolish child poverty.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动旨在消除儿童贫困。
senses.why: The word stretches from written rules to conditions that are imagined as unwanted structures to be torn down.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从成文规则扩展到被想象成该拆除的多余结构的那种状况。

senses.title: To close an office
senses.definition: to do away with an institution, post, or office
senses.definitionCN: 取消某个机构、职位或职务
senses.example: The new government abolished the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 新政府撤销了这个部。
senses.why: An office is an arrangement that can be cancelled; abolishing it leaves no post for anyone to hold.
senses.whyCN: 职位是一种可以取消的安排；废除它之后，就没有位置可让人担任。

senses.title: To remove an abstract evil
senses.definition: to put a complete end to something abstract and harmful
senses.definitionCN: 彻底终结某种抽象而有害的事物
senses.example: They hoped to abolish inequality in hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们希望彻底消除招聘中的不平等。
senses.why: Abstract evils are pictured as marks on a clean surface, and abolishing them restores the surface.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的恶被想象成干净表面上的污迹，消除它们就是让表面恢复洁净。

senses.title: To declare something void
senses.definition: to declare formally that something no longer exists or applies
senses.definitionCN: 正式宣布某事物不再存在或不再适用
senses.example: The treaty abolished the old border controls.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约取消了旧的边境管制。
senses.why: The legal act of declaring an end is the source of all the other senses: once declared void, a thing cannot be used again.
senses.whyCN: 「宣布终止」这一法律行为是所有其他义项的源头：一旦被宣告失效，事物就不能再被使用。

intro.en: Abolish comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to destroy or wipe out', and its deeper origin is disputed.
intro.cn: abolish 来自一个意为「摧毁、抹去」的拉丁语动词，它更早的来源存在争议。

items.en: The internal history of Latin abolere is disputed; one old suggestion links the second element to a verb for growing, but this is not settled.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abolere 的内部历史存在争议；一种古老推测把后一成分与表示「生长」的动词联系起来，但尚无定论。

items.en: abolere meant 'to destroy, efface, wipe out', and it was used of marks, customs, and institutions.
items.cn: abolere 意为「摧毁、抹去、消除」，可用于记号、习俗与制度。

items.en: The noun abolitio named the act of cancelling or annulling something.
items.cn: 名词 abolitio 指取消或废止某事物的行为。

items.en: Old French abolir carried the legal sense of repealing a law or custom.
items.cn: 古法语 abolir 带有废除法律或习俗的法律含义。

items.en: English abolish is recorded from the fifteenth century, mainly in legal contexts.
items.cn: 英语 abolish 自十五世纪有记录，主要用于法律语境。

items.en: Modern usage extends the verb from laws and institutions to poverty, inequality, and other social conditions.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个动词从法律与制度扩展到贫困、不平等及其他社会状况。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, the person, and the adjective from the same family; the second gathers verbs for cancelling something formally.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的名词、人物与形容词；第二组收表示正式取消的动词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning the official ending of a law, system, or practice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废除、废止」，指法律、制度或做法的正式终止。

entries.definition: A person who campaigns for the abolition of a practice, especially slavery.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废奴主义者」，指主张废除某种做法、尤指奴隶制的人。

entries.definition: A person or thing that abolishes something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废除者」，指废除某事物的人或物。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning capable of being abolished.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可废除的」。

entries.definition: To cancel a law formally by a legislative act.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「废止、撤销」，通过立法正式取消一项法律。

entries.definition: To cancel a right, licence, or decision officially.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撤销、吊销」，正式取消权利、执照或决定。

entries.definition: To declare a marriage, contract, or result invalid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣告无效」，指宣布婚姻、合同或结果无效。

entries.definition: To destroy something harmful completely, especially disease.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「根除」，彻底消灭有害事物，尤指疾病。

entries.definition: To remove or get rid of something completely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「消除、排除」，彻底去除某物。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the great historical collocations and the noun family; the abstract hooks picture the sign being taken down.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用重要的历史搭配与名词词族；抽象记忆点想象牌子被摘下的画面。

normal.en: Abolish slavery is the most famous historical collocation of the verb.
normal.cn: abolish slavery 是这个动词最著名的历史搭配。

normal.en: Abolish a law, a tax, or the death penalty are standard public-policy collocations.
normal.cn: abolish a law、abolish a tax、abolish the death penalty 都是标准公共政策搭配。

normal.en: Abolition is the noun, and an abolitionist campaigns for it.
normal.cn: 名词是 abolition，主张废除的人叫 abolitionist。

normal.en: The -ish ending marks a verb, as in establish and punish.
normal.cn: -ish 结尾标明动词，如 establish 与 punish。

normal.en: The word can move from written rules to social evils such as poverty.
normal.cn: 这个词可以从成文规则扩展到贫困等社会弊病。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden sign with old rules being pulled down and split.
abstract.cn: 想象一块写着旧规矩的木牌被拉下、劈开。

abstract.en: Picture a line of text wiped from a page until the paper is clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一行字从纸页上被擦掉，直到纸面干净。

abstract.en: Picture a locked gate taken off its hinges so no one can close it again.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门被从铰链上卸下，再也没人能把它关上。

examples.en: The country abolished slavery in the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 这个国家在十九世纪废除了奴隶制。

examples.en: They want to abolish the tax on books.
examples.cn: 他们想取消图书税。

examples.en: The old rule was abolished last year.
examples.cn: 那条旧规定去年被废除了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额波利什」——把旧规矩写在一块牌子上，当众一摘一劈，从此不再作数。

root: 拉丁语 abolere（摧毁、抹去）+ 法语 -ir，经古法语 abolir 进入英语；核心义是「把成文的规矩彻底抹掉」

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from repealing written laws and systems, through customs and practices, to abolishing institutions and abstract social evils.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从废止成文法律与制度，经过习俗与做法，走到撤销机构与消除抽象的社会弊病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old rule board pulled down and broken in public
core.cn: 核心意象：一块旧规矩牌被当众摘下并劈碎

branches.en: Written law and standing systems are formally ended.
branches.cn: 成文法律与长期制度被正式终止。

branches.en: Customs and daily practices stop being observed.
branches.cn: 习俗与日常做法不再被遵行。

branches.en: Social evils and abstract harms are wiped out.
branches.cn: 社会弊病与抽象伤害被彻底消除。

branches.en: Institutions and offices are closed or cancelled.
branches.cn: 机构与职位被关闭或取消。

branches.en: A formal declaration makes something void.
branches.cn: 正式宣告使某事物失效。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem abol-, the verb ending -ish, and the noun and agent endings -ition and -ist.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 abol-、动词后缀 -ish，以及名词与施动者后缀 -ition、-ist 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin abolere and abolitio are the direct source of abolish and abolition, so the Latin entries record the verb and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abolere 与 abolitio 是 abolish 与 abolition 的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其名词。

items.meaning: present tense with he, she, or it

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「废除；废止」
名词，义为「废奴主义者；主张废除者」

definition_zh: 土著的；原住民的；土生的；原始的
definition_en: belonging to the people or species that were present in a place from the earliest times
core_image: 从土地最深处长出来的第一代人，脚与泥土连在一起
scene: 博物馆的展柜里摆着世代居住在河谷的人使用过的工具。The exhibition honours the aboriginal people of the river valley.
sceneCN: 这里 aboriginal 是「原住民的」（第 1 个义项：最早居住在某地的人群）；句意为展览致敬河谷的原住民。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词后缀构成，义为「原住民；土著居民」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「最初地；原初地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「原初性；本土性」

senses.title: Of a land's first peoples
senses.definition: belonging to the peoples who lived in a region before others arrived
senses.definitionCN: 属于在其他群体到来之前就居住于某地的人群
senses.example: The museum works with aboriginal communities.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆与原住民社群合作。
senses.why: Latin ab origine means 'from the beginning'; the people who were there from the beginning are named by that phrase.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ab origine 意为「从最初开始」；从一开始就在那里的人，正是由这个短语命名的。

senses.title: Native to a region
senses.definition: of a plant or animal, native to a place rather than introduced
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物原产于某地，而非外来引入
senses.example: The park protects several aboriginal species.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园保护着几种本土物种。
senses.why: The 'from the beginning' idea applies to living things as well: a species that was there first is aboriginal to the land.
senses.whyCN: 「从最初开始」的观念也适用于生物：最早就在那里的物种，对这片土地而言就是土生的。

senses.title: Original and earliest
senses.definition: existing from the earliest period, before later changes
senses.definitionCN: 存在于最早时期、早于后来变化的
senses.example: The study traces aboriginal forms of the language.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追溯这种语言最早的形式。
senses.why: Anything that dates from the beginning can be called aboriginal, including ideas and language forms.
senses.whyCN: 任何始于最初的事物都可称为 aboriginal，包括观念与语言形式。

senses.title: Of Aboriginal Australia
senses.definition: relating to the Indigenous peoples of Australia
senses.definitionCN: 与澳大利亚原住民族群有关的
senses.example: She studies aboriginal art from the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究北部的原住民艺术。
senses.why: In Australian English the capitalized Aboriginal is the standard term for the continent's first peoples.
senses.whyCN: 在澳大利亚英语中，大写的 Aboriginal 是称呼该大陆最早居民的通用术语。

senses.title: Of a native culture
senses.definition: belonging to the culture of a place's first inhabitants
senses.definitionCN: 属于某地最早居民的文化
senses.example: The festival celebrates aboriginal traditions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日庆祝原住民传统。
senses.why: Culture is one of the things a first people carries, so the adjective naturally attaches to its songs, stories, and rites.
senses.whyCN: 文化是原住民族所承载的事物之一，因此这个形容词自然附着于他们的歌谣、故事与仪式。

senses.title: Growing in its native range
senses.definition: growing naturally in the area where it evolved
senses.definitionCN: 在它演化所在的地区自然生长
senses.example: These aboriginal grasses survive long droughts.
senses.exampleCN: 这些原生草种能挺过漫长干旱。
senses.why: A plant that has always grown in a region is a first inhabitant of that soil, and the word borrows the human image.
senses.whyCN: 一直在某地生长的植物，是那片土壤最早的居民，这个词借用了人的意象。

senses.title: Inherited from early ancestors
senses.definition: coming from the earliest ancestors of a group
senses.definitionCN: 来自某个群体最早的祖先
senses.example: The elders keep aboriginal knowledge of the seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 长者们保存着祖先传下的季节知识。
senses.why: Knowledge that passes from the first inhabitants is treated as part of the same inheritance.
senses.whyCN: 从最早居民传下来的知识，被视为同一份遗产的一部分。

senses.title: Untouched and original
senses.definition: describing a landscape or condition before outside change
senses.definitionCN: 形容在外部改变之前的地貌或状态
senses.example: The valley remains in its aboriginal state.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷仍保持原始状态。
senses.why: Landscapes untouched by later settlement are imagined as still standing at the beginning.
senses.whyCN: 未被后来定居改变的地貌，被想象成仍停在最初的样子。

intro.en: Aboriginal is built directly from a Latin phrase meaning 'from the beginning', and it preserves that phrase almost transparently.
intro.cn: aboriginal 直接由意为「从最初开始」的拉丁短语构成，几乎透明地保留了那个短语。

items.en: ab is a Latin preposition meaning 'from, away from'.
items.cn: ab 是拉丁语介词，意为「从、离开」。

items.en: origo meant 'a beginning, source, birth'; it also produced origin and original.
items.cn: origo 意为「开端、源头、出生」，也衍生出 origin 与 original。

items.en: The phrase ab origine, 'from the beginning', was used of peoples and things present from the first.
items.cn: 短语 ab origine 意为「从最初开始」，用于从一开始就存在的人群与事物。

items.en: The plural Aborigines named the first inhabitants of a region in Roman writing.
items.cn: 复数 Aborigines 在罗马文献中指某地最早的居民。

items.en: English aboriginal appears in the seventeenth century as an adjective for the earliest inhabitants.
items.cn: 英语 aboriginal 在十七世纪出现，作形容词指最早的居民。

items.en: The term spread to botany, geology, and Australian usage, where Aboriginal names the continent's first peoples.
items.cn: 这个术语扩展到植物学、地质学与澳大利亚用法；在那里，Aboriginal 指该大陆最早的居民。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and related origin words; the second gathers adjectives for what was there first.
note.cn: 第一组收名词、副词与相关的「起源」词；第二组收表示「最早就在那里」的形容词。

entries.definition: A member of the first people of a region; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「原住民、土著居民」，是形容词背后的名词形式。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'from the beginning or in the original state'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「最初地、原初地」。

entries.definition: The quality of being original to a place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「原初性、本土性」，指属于某地原初事物的性质。

entries.definition: The point where something begins; from the same Latin noun origo.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「起源」，来自同一个拉丁名词 origo。

entries.definition: Born or growing naturally in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「土生土长的、原产的」，指在某地自然出生或生长。

entries.definition: Belonging to a place by birth or natural growth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「本地的、天生的」，指因出生或自然生长而属于某地。

entries.definition: Existing from the start, before copies or changes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的、原来的」，指在复制或改变之前就存在。

entries.definition: Belonging to an early stage of development.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「原始的」，指属于发展的早期阶段。

entries.definition: Coming before all others in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最早的、第一的」，在时间或顺序上先于其他。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks work from the Latin phrase ab origine and the common policy collocations; the abstract hooks picture the first feet on the land.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点来自拉丁短语 ab origine 与常见政策搭配；抽象记忆点想象最早踏上这片土地的脚。

normal.en: Aboriginal is literally ab origine, 'from the beginning'.
normal.cn: aboriginal 字面就是 ab origine，即「从最初开始」。

normal.en: Aboriginal people and aboriginal rights are standard public-policy phrases.
normal.cn: aboriginal people 与 aboriginal rights 是标准公共政策短语。

normal.en: Origin, original, and aboriginal all share the Latin noun origo.
normal.cn: origin、original 与 aboriginal 都共享拉丁名词 origo。

normal.en: In Australian English, Aboriginal with a capital letter names the continent's first peoples.
normal.cn: 在澳大利亚英语中，大写的 Aboriginal 指该大陆最早的居民。

normal.en: The adjective also works for plants and landscapes that were there first.
normal.cn: 这个形容词也适用于最早就在那里的植物与地貌。

abstract.en: Picture bare feet pressing into soil that no one else has walked on.
abstract.cn: 想象赤脚踩进无人走过的泥土。

abstract.en: Picture a seed already in the ground before any fence is built.
abstract.cn: 想象围栏尚未建起，种子早已在土里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand painting the same pattern that ancestors painted on rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手画出祖先曾画在岩石上的同一个图案。

examples.en: The law recognizes aboriginal land rights.
examples.cn: 法律承认原住民的土地权利。

examples.en: Several aboriginal languages are endangered.
examples.cn: 几种原住民语言濒临消亡。

examples.en: The valley still holds aboriginal forest.
examples.cn: 这个山谷仍保有原始森林。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿伯瑞金诺」——阿伯一出生就在这片土地上，脚底沾着最原始的泥。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with the first peoples, then extend to native species, earliest forms, Australian usage, culture, plants, inherited knowledge, and untouched landscapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从最早的居民开始，扩展到本土物种、最早形式、澳大利亚用法、文化、植物、祖传知识与未开发的地貌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first feet standing on untouched ground
core.cn: 核心意象：最早踏上未动过的土地的双脚

branches.en: Human first peoples, including the capitalized Australian term.
branches.cn: 人类中最早的居民，包括澳大利亚的大写用法。

branches.en: Plants and animals native to a place from the start.
branches.cn: 从一开始就原产于某地的动植物。

branches.en: Earliest forms of language and knowledge passed down.
branches.cn: 传下来的最早语言形式与知识。

branches.en: The culture carried by a place's first inhabitants.
branches.cn: 某地最早居民所承载的文化。

branches.en: Landscapes still in their original, unchanged state.
branches.cn: 仍保持原初、未被改变的地貌。

intro.en: The word is transparently built from the Latin preposition ab and the noun origo, with the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁介词 ab、名词 origo 与形容词后缀 -al 透明地构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin origo and ab origine are the direct source of the English word, so the Latin entries record the phrase and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 origo 与短语 ab origine 是英语词的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录这个短语及其名词。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「原住民；土著居民」
副词，义为「最初地；原初地」

definition_zh: 不成功的；夭折的；中途失败的；发育不全的
definition_en: failing to achieve its purpose, or coming to an end before completion
core_image: 刚点火的火箭在半空断成两截，落回地面
scene: 队伍在山口折返，暴风雪让这次突袭彻底落空。The abortive raid ended before the troops reached the pass.
sceneCN: 这里 abortive 是「中途失败的」（第 1 个义项：行动未达目的便告终止）；句意为这次突袭在部队抵达山口前就失败了。

pos.zh: （医学）顿挫的；（生物学）发育不全的

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词后缀构成，义为「中止；流产」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「流产；中止」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「失败地；中途终止地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「失败性；夭折状态」

senses.title: Failing to reach its aim
senses.definition: of an action or attempt, ending in failure before its goal is reached
senses.definitionCN: 指行动或尝试在达到目标之前以失败告终
senses.example: The rescue was an abortive attempt.
senses.exampleCN: 这次救援是一次失败的尝试。
senses.why: Latin aboriri meant 'to miscarry', from ab- 'away' and oriri 'to be born'; an abortive action is one whose outcome never comes to birth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aboriri 意为「流产」，由 ab-（离开）与 oriri（出生）构成；abortive 的行动就是结果从未「出生」的行动。

senses.title: Of a plan that collapses
senses.definition: of a plan or scheme, failing before it can be carried out
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或方案在付诸实施前就失败
senses.example: Their abortive plan cost the company a fortune.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夭折的计划让公司损失了一大笔钱。
senses.why: A plan is expected to be 'born' in action; if it collapses early, it is abortive in the same obstetrical image.
senses.whyCN: 计划本应在行动中「诞生」；若早早崩解，就同样落入这个产科意象，成为 abortive。

senses.title: Of a revolt that fails
senses.definition: describing a uprising or coup that is put down or collapses
senses.definitionCN: 形容被镇压或自行瓦解的起义或政变
senses.example: The abortive uprising lasted only two days.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失败的起义只持续了两天。
senses.why: A revolt is an attempted birth of a new order; crushed before it takes hold, it earns the word.
senses.whyCN: 起义是试图让新秩序「诞生」；在站稳之前被压碎，就得到这个词。

senses.title: Of medical treatment
senses.definition: describing treatment that stops a disease in its early stage
senses.definitionCN: 形容在疾病早期将其截断的治疗
senses.example: Doctors used abortive treatment to shorten the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用顿挫疗法缩短病程。
senses.why: Medicine keeps the 'cut short' sense literally: the treatment aborts the disease's course.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了字面的「截断」义：这种治疗把疾病的进程截断。

senses.title: Of an organ that never develops
senses.definition: of a body part, remaining small and non-functional
senses.definitionCN: 指身体部位保持很小且无功能
senses.example: The whale retains an abortive hind limb.
senses.exampleCN: 鲸保留着一条发育不全的后肢。
senses.why: Biology borrows the image of a process that stops before completion: the organ's growth is aborted.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了「过程未完成便停止」的意象：这个器官的生长被中止了。

senses.title: Of a pregnancy that ends early
senses.definition: describing a pregnancy or birth process that ends before it can continue
senses.definitionCN: 形容在继续之前就终止的妊娠或生产进程
senses.example: The term abortive is used for therapies that prevent a pregnancy from continuing.
senses.exampleCN: abortive 一词用于阻止妊娠继续的疗法。
senses.why: This is the literal source of the word: a process that should have led to birth stops on the way.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最字面的来源：本应导向出生的过程在中途停下。

senses.title: Of an effort that comes to nothing
senses.definition: of work or effort, producing no lasting result
senses.definitionCN: 指工作或努力没有产生持久结果
senses.example: All their abortive efforts left the bridge unbuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 他们所有徒劳的努力都没能让桥建成。
senses.why: Effort is expected to give birth to a result; when nothing is delivered, the effort is abortive.
senses.whyCN: 努力本应「生出」结果；当什么也没产出时，这份努力就是 abortive。

senses.title: Of a movement that stops short
senses.titleCN: 中途停止的运动或进程
senses.definition: of a process or movement, halting before its natural end
senses.definitionCN: 指进程或运动在自然结束前停下
senses.example: The reform was an abortive move that changed nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革是一次中途停止、什么也没改变的举动。
senses.why: The general sense is simply 'cut off before completion', the widest extension of the original image.
senses.whyCN: 最一般的义项就是「在完成前被截断」，这是原初意象最宽的延伸。

intro.en: Abortive comes from the Latin verb for miscarrying, whose parts mean 'away' and 'to be born'.
intro.cn: abortive 来自表示「流产」的拉丁语动词，其成分意为「离开」与「出生」。

items.en: oriri meant 'to rise, appear, be born'; it also produced origin and orient.
items.cn: oriri 意为「升起、出现、出生」，也衍生出 origin 与 orient。

items.en: ab is the preposition 'from, away from'.
items.cn: ab 是介词，意为「从、离开」。

items.en: aboriri meant 'to miscarry, fail to be born', built from ab- and oriri.
items.cn: aboriri 意为「流产、未能出生」，由 ab- 与 oriri 构成。

items.en: The past participle abortus gave the noun for a miscarriage and the adjective abortivus.
items.cn: 过去分词 abortus 构成表示流产的名词，并衍生出形容词 abortivus。

items.en: English adopted abortive first in the medical sense and then for any failed enterprise.
items.cn: 英语先吸收 abortive 的医学义，随后用于任何失败的事业。

items.en: Modern usage applies the word to plans, revolts, efforts, and underdeveloped organs.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词用于计划、起义、努力与发育不全的器官。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, noun, and adverb from the same family; the second gathers adjectives for failure and futility.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的动词、名词与副词；第二组收表示失败与徒劳的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to stop a process before it finishes.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「中止、流产」，指在完成前停止某个过程。

entries.definition: The noun for the ending of a pregnancy or the failure of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「流产；中止」，指妊娠终止或进程失败。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in a failed or cut-short way'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「失败地、中途终止地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being abortive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「失败性、夭折状态」。

entries.definition: Not achieving the intended result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不成功的」，未达到预期结果。

entries.definition: Useless because it cannot produce a result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「徒劳的」，因无法产生结果而无用。

entries.definition: Producing no useful outcome, like a tree with no fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无成果的」，像不结果的树一样没有有用产出。

entries.definition: Having not succeeded in what was attempted.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「失败的」，在尝试的事情上没有成功。

entries.definition: Producing no result despite effort.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「徒然的」，尽管努力却没有结果。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the obstetrical image behind the word and the standard collocations; the abstract hooks picture a process cut off midway.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用词后的产科意象与标准搭配；抽象记忆点想象中途被截断的过程。

normal.en: Abortive and abort share the Latin image of a birth that does not happen.
normal.cn: abortive 与 abort 共享「未能出生的生产」这一拉丁意象。

normal.en: An abortive attempt, an abortive coup, and an abortive plan are standard collocations.
normal.cn: an abortive attempt、an abortive coup、an abortive plan 都是标准搭配。

normal.en: Abortive treatment is a medical phrase for stopping a disease early.
normal.cn: abortive treatment 是医学术语，指早期截断疾病。

normal.en: Abortive organ describes a body part that never fully develops.
normal.cn: abortive organ 指从未完全发育的身体部位。

normal.en: The -ive ending turns the action into a quality: what fails is abortive.
normal.cn: -ive 结尾把动作变成性质：失败的东西就是 abortive。

abstract.en: Picture a rocket that breaks apart in mid-air and falls back to the pad.
abstract.cn: 想象火箭在半空断成两截，落回发射台。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge half built, then abandoned with its arches open to the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一座建到一半就被放弃的桥，拱架空对天空。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that sprouts, then withers before the first leaf opens.
abstract.cn: 想象种子发了芽，却在第一片叶子展开前枯萎。

examples.en: The attack was abortive and the troops withdrew.
examples.cn: 进攻失败，部队撤退了。

examples.en: They made an abortive attempt to reach the summit.
examples.cn: 他们尝试登顶，但未能成功。

examples.en: The plan proved abortive from the start.
examples.cn: 这个计划从一开始就注定失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额波提夫」——火箭刚升空就断成两截，任务没出生就落了地。

sensesIntro.en: The senses grow from the literal image of a birth that does not happen, then spread to plans, revolts, efforts, medical treatment, and underdeveloped organs.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从「未能出生」的字面意象生长出来，再扩展到计划、起义、努力、医学治疗与发育不全的器官。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a process cut off before it can be born
core.cn: 核心意象：一个在「出生」前就被截断的过程

branches.en: Attempts, plans, and efforts that produce no result.
branches.cn: 尝试、计划与努力没有产生结果。

branches.en: A revolt or coup that is crushed before it takes hold.
branches.cn: 起义或政变在站稳前被压碎。

branches.en: Medical processes stopped early, including the literal pregnancy sense.
branches.cn: 医学过程被早期截断，包括字面的妊娠义。

branches.en: An organ whose growth stops before it can function.
branches.cn: 器官在具备功能前停止生长。

branches.en: The general sense of any movement halting before its natural end.
branches.cn: 任何运动在自然结束前停下的普遍义。

intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 abort-、形容词后缀 -ive，以及周围的名词与动词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin aboriri and abortus are the direct source of abort and abortive, so the Latin entries record the verb and its participle.

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「中止；流产」
名词，义为「流产；中止」

definition_zh: 大量存在；充满；富于；盛产
definition_en: to exist in large numbers or quantities, or to be full of something
core_image: 水从容器边缘漫出来，四周到处都是
scene: 雨后的草坡上，蘑菇一丛丛冒出来。Mushrooms abound on the wet hillside after rain.
sceneCN: 这里 abound 是「大量存在」（第 1 个义项：某物数量很多地出现）；句意为雨后湿润的山坡上蘑菇大量生长。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「丰富；充裕」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「丰富的；大量的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「丰富地；大量地」

senses.title: To exist in large numbers
senses.definition: of things, to be present in large numbers or quantities
senses.definitionCN: 指事物以很大的数量出现
senses.example: Wild flowers abound in this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷里野花繁盛。
senses.why: Latin abundare meant 'to overflow'; what abounds is so plentiful that it spills over the edges of the container.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abundare 意为「溢出」；abound 的东西多到从容器边缘漫出来。

senses.title: To be rich in something
senses.definition: to have a great deal of a particular quality or thing
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量的某种性质或事物
senses.example: The region abounds in mineral resources.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区矿产资源丰富。
senses.why: A place that overflows with a resource is described with in or with, the container and its contents named together.
senses.whyCN: 一个充满某种资源的地方用 in 或 with 来连接，容器与内容被一起说出。

senses.title: Of animals: to be numerous
senses.definition: of animals or plants, to occur in great numbers in a habitat
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物在某一栖息地大量出现
senses.example: Deer abound in these forests.
senses.exampleCN: 这些森林里鹿群众多。
senses.why: Living things that fill a habitat are pictured as filling a vessel to overflowing.
senses.whyCN: 填满栖息地的生物，被想象成把容器装到溢出。

senses.title: Of talk or rumour: to circulate widely
senses.definition: of stories, rumours, or ideas, to be widespread
senses.definitionCN: 指说法、传闻或观念广泛流传
senses.example: Rumours abound about the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 关于合并的传闻四起。
senses.why: Words and stories can also overflow a community, spreading faster than anyone can count.
senses.whyCN: 话语与故事也会漫过一个社群，传播得比谁数得都快。

senses.title: Of a place: to produce plentifully
senses.definition: of a region or farm, to yield large crops or products
senses.definitionCN: 指地区或农场产出大量作物或产品
senses.example: The orchards abound with apples in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天果园里苹果累累。
senses.why: The overflow image turns agricultural: the harvest is more than the baskets can hold.
senses.whyCN: 溢出的意象转向农业：收成多到篮子装不下。

senses.title: To be filled with problems
senses.definition: to be full of something undesirable, such as errors or complaints
senses.definitionCN: 充满不想要的东西，如错误或抱怨
senses.example: The report abounds with errors.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告错误百出。
senses.why: The same 'full to overflowing' pattern works for defects, which crowd a text as water crowds a jar.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「满到溢出」结构也适用于缺陷，它们挤满文本，像水挤满罐子。

senses.title: Of resources: to be plentiful
senses.definition: of resources or supplies, to be available in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: 指资源或供给以大量形式存在
senses.example: Clean water abounds in the northern valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 北部山谷中清洁水源充裕。
senses.why: Plenty is measured as volume: a resource that abounds is one whose supply spills past demand.
senses.whyCN: 充裕以体量来衡量：abound 的资源就是供给溢过需求。

senses.title: Of ideas: to spring up
senses.definition: of ideas or possibilities, to appear in great number
senses.definitionCN: 指想法或可能性大量出现
senses.example: New ideas abound at the start of a project.
senses.exampleCN: 项目开始时新想法层出不穷。
senses.why: Abstract things are imagined as a flow that rises and spreads, so an active period is one where ideas abound.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事物被想象成上涨漫开的流，因此活跃时期就是想法 abound 的时期。

intro.en: Abound comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to overflow', built from a prefix and the word for a wave.
intro.cn: abound 来自一个意为「溢出」的拉丁语动词，由前缀与表示「波浪」的词构成。

items.en: The root *wed- is reconstructed with the sense 'water'; it also lies behind English water and wet.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *wed- 被重构为「水」之义；英语 water 与 wet 也源自它。

items.en: unda meant 'a wave, water', and it produced undulate and inundate.
items.cn: unda 意为「波浪、水」，衍生出 undulate 与 inundate。

items.en: undare meant 'to rise in waves, flow', a verb of water moving in volume.
items.cn: undare 意为「波浪涌起、流动」，是一个表示水大量运动的动词。

items.en: ab- 'away, from' plus undare formed abundare, 'to overflow, be plentiful'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 undare 构成 abundare，意为「溢出、丰盛」。

items.en: Old French abonder carried the sense 'to be plentiful' into medieval use.
items.cn: 古法语 abonder 把「丰盛」之义带入中世纪用法。

items.en: English abound keeps the two patterns abound in and abound with, and extends to rumours, errors, and ideas.
items.cn: 英语 abound 保留 abound in 与 abound with 两种结构，并扩展到传闻、错误与想法。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adjective, and adverb from the same family, plus two water-root words; the second gathers verbs for being plentiful.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的名词、形容词与副词，以及两个同「水」词根的词；第二组收表示丰盛的动词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning a very large quantity of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「丰富、充裕」，指某物数量极大。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning existing in large quantities.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「丰富的、大量的」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'plentifully or very clearly'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「丰富地、大量地」，也可表示「十分清楚地」。

entries.definition: To flood or overwhelm, from the Latin word for a wave.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「淹没、使应接不暇」，来自表示波浪的拉丁词。

entries.definition: To move in waves, from the same Latin noun unda.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「波动、起伏」，来自同一个拉丁名词 unda。

entries.definition: To be full of things, especially living things, moving in great numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「充满、涌动」，尤指大量生物活动。

entries.definition: To move or gather in large numbers, like bees.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「成群移动、蜂拥」，像蜜蜂一样大量聚集。

entries.definition: To increase rapidly in number.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激增、迅速繁殖」。

entries.definition: To grow or develop well and plentifully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「繁茂、兴旺」，生长或发展得很好很多。

entries.definition: To be so full that contents spill over.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「溢出」，满到内容物漫出。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the two fixed patterns abound in and abound with and the water image; the abstract hooks picture the overflow.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 abund in 与 abound with 两个固定结构及水的意象；抽象记忆点想象溢出。

normal.en: Abound in and abound with are the two patterns; in names the place, with names the contents.
normal.cn: abound in 与 abound with 是两个结构；in 引出地点，with 引出内容。

normal.en: Abundance is the noun and abundant the adjective, both from the same overflow image.
normal.cn: 名词是 abundance，形容词是 abundant，二者都来自同一个「溢出」意象。

normal.en: Rumours abound and opportunities abound are common news and business phrases.
normal.cn: rumours abound 与 opportunities abound 是常见新闻与商业短语。

normal.en: The Latin source is undare, 'to flow in waves', so abound is water overflowing a rim.
normal.cn: 拉丁来源是 undare（波浪流动），因此 abound 就是水漫过边缘。

normal.en: The -s form abounds is used with singular subjects such as wildlife.
normal.cn: -s 形式 abounds 与 wildlife 等单数主语连用。

abstract.en: Picture a barrel filled until water runs down its sides.
abstract.cn: 想象木桶被装到水从桶壁流下。

abstract.en: Picture mushrooms pushing up through wet grass in every direction.
abstract.cn: 想象蘑菇从湿润的草丛里向四面八方冒出来。

abstract.en: Picture a room so full of talking people that voices spill into the street.
abstract.cn: 想象房间挤满说话的人，声音漫到街上。

examples.en: Fish abound in these cold rivers.
examples.cn: 这些寒冷的河流里鱼群繁多。

examples.en: The internet abounds with misleading claims.
examples.cn: 网络上充斥着误导性说法。

examples.en: Examples of this pattern abound in the corpus.
examples.cn: 这种模式的例子在语料库中大量存在。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额邦德」——桶里的水装得太满，沿着桶边到处流，东西多得到处都是。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ undare（波浪流动、涌），构成 abundare（溢出）；核心义是「多到漫出容器」

sensesIntro.en: The senses all grow from 'overflow': things, animals, words, crops, resources, and ideas can all fill a space past its edges.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都从「溢出」生长出来：事物、动物、言语、作物、资源与想法，都能把空间装到漫出边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water running over the rim of a full vessel
core.cn: 核心意象：水从装满的容器边缘漫出

branches.en: Things, animals, and crops fill a place beyond counting.
branches.cn: 事物、动物与作物把一处空间装到数不清。

branches.en: A place or supply is rich in a resource, named with in or with.
branches.cn: 某地或供给富于某种资源，用 in 或 with 引出。

branches.en: Words and rumours fill a community and spread widely.
branches.cn: 言语与传闻充满社群并广泛传播。

branches.en: Undesirable things such as errors crowd a text.
branches.cn: 错误等不想要的东西挤满文本。

branches.en: Ideas rise and spread in an active period.
branches.cn: 在活跃时期，想法涌起并扩散。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem abund-, the noun ending -ance, and the adjective and adverb endings -ant and -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 abund-、名词后缀 -ance，以及形容词与副词后缀 -ant、-ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin abundare and unda are the direct source of abound and its family, so the Latin entries record both the verb and the wave noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abundare 与 unda 是 abound 及其词族的直接来源，因此拉丁条目同时记录动词与「波浪」名词。

items.meaning: present tense with he, she, or it

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「丰富；充裕」
形容词，义为「丰富的；大量的」

definition_zh: 删节；节略；缩短；削减
definition_en: to shorten a text, speech, or right by removing part of it
core_image: 把一本厚书压薄，只留下主干
scene: 出版社把厚厚的回忆录压成一本小书。The publisher decided to abridge the memoir for younger readers.
sceneCN: 这里 abridge 是「删节」（第 1 个义项：删去部分内容使篇幅缩短）；句意为出版社决定为年轻读者删节这本回忆录。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「删节；节略本」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「删节；节略本」，是另一种拼写
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「删节过的；简略的」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「删节者」

senses.title: To shorten a book
senses.definition: to shorten a book or article by removing less essential parts
senses.definitionCN: 删去较不重要的部分，使书或文章变短
senses.example: The publisher decided to abridge the memoir.
senses.exampleCN: 出版社决定对这本回忆录作删节。
senses.why: Late Latin abbreviare meant 'to shorten', from brevis 'short'; an abridged book keeps its trunk and loses some branches.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 abbreviare 意为「使变短」，来自 brevis（短的）；删节过的书保留主干，去掉一些枝叶。

senses.title: To cut a speech short
senses.definition: to reduce the length of a speech or performance
senses.definitionCN: 减少演讲或表演的长度
senses.example: The speaker had to abridge her talk to ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲者不得不把讲话压缩到十分钟。
senses.why: Time limits force the same pruning: the essential points stay and the rest is cut away.
senses.whyCN: 时间限制迫使同样的修剪：要点留下，其余被剪掉。

senses.title: To condense a text
senses.definition: to present a text in a shorter form while keeping its main content
senses.definitionCN: 以更短的形式呈现文本，同时保留主要内容
senses.example: They abridged the report into a two-page summary.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把报告压缩成两页摘要。
senses.why: Condensing is the positive side of shortening: the trunk is kept, and only the side growth is removed.
senses.whyCN: 压缩是缩短的积极一面：主干保留，只去掉侧枝。

senses.title: To curtail a right
senses.definition: to reduce or limit a legal right or freedom
senses.definitionCN: 减少或限制某项法定权利或自由
senses.example: The new rules abridge the right to protest.
senses.exampleCN: 新规削减了抗议的权利。
senses.why: A right is treated as a long document that can be cut down, which is why the word carries a legal warning.
senses.whyCN: 权利被当作一份可以被删短的长文件，因此这个词带有法律警告的意味。

senses.title: To shorten a period
senses.definition: to make a period of time shorter
senses.definitionCN: 使一段时间变短
senses.example: The fast route abridges the journey by an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这条快路把旅程缩短了一小时。
senses.why: Distance and time are imagined as a long text that can be trimmed at the edges.
senses.whyCN: 距离与时间被想象成一份可以从边缘裁短的长文本。

senses.title: To make a place feel shorter
senses.definition: to shorten the perceived length of a route or wait
senses.definitionCN: 使路线或等待在感觉上变短
senses.example: Good company abridges a long wait.
senses.exampleCN: 有好的同伴，漫长的等待也会显得短些。
senses.why: The metaphor extends to experience: what fills the time pleasantly cuts its felt length.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻延伸到体验：愉快地填满时间的东西，会削减时间的感受长度。

senses.title: To produce an abridged edition
senses.definition: to prepare a shortened edition for a particular readership
senses.definitionCN: 为特定读者群准备缩短的版本
senses.example: The school abridged the novel for class use.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为课堂使用删节了这部小说。
senses.why: Publishing turns the action into a product: the abridged edition is the shortened trunk made portable.
senses.whyCN: 出版把动作变成产品：节略本就是被缩短、便于携带的主干。

senses.title: To reduce a privilege
senses.definition: to take away part of a privilege or benefit
senses.definitionCN: 拿走某项特权或利益的一部分
senses.example: The treaty abridged the company's trading privileges.
senses.exampleCN: 条约缩减了该公司的贸易特权。
senses.why: Privileges are long lists of benefits; abridging them cuts entries from the list without erasing it.
senses.whyCN: 特权是一长串利益；削减它们就是从清单上删去条目，而不是整份撕掉。

intro.en: Abridge goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to shorten', built on the adjective for short.
intro.cn: abridge 可追溯到意为「使变短」的拉丁语动词，其基础是表示「短」的形容词。

items.en: brevis meant 'short', and it produced brevity, brief, and abbreviate.
items.cn: brevis 意为「短的」，衍生出 brevity、brief 与 abbreviate。

items.en: abbreviare meant 'to shorten', formed with ad- and brevis.
items.cn: abbreviare 意为「使变短」，由 ad- 与 brevis 构成。

items.en: Old French abregier carried the sense 'to shorten a text or a period'.
items.cn: 古法语 abregier 带有「缩短文本或时段」之义。

items.en: English abregen appears in the Middle English period with the same sense.
items.cn: 英语 abregen 在中古英语时期出现，含义相同。

items.en: The modern spelling abridge settled later, and the legal sense 'to curtail a right' developed alongside the textual one.
items.cn: 现代拼写 abridge 较晚才固定下来；「削减权利」的法律义与文本义同时发展。

items.en: The noun has two spellings, abridgement and abridgment, both in standard use.
items.cn: 名词有 abridgement 与 abridgment 两种拼写，二者都是标准用法。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adjective, and agent forms from the same family; the second gathers verbs for making something shorter.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的名词、形容词与施动者形式；第二组收表示使某物变短的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a shortened version of a text.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「删节、节略本」，指文本的缩短版本。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning shortened by removing parts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「删节过的、简略的」。

entries.definition: A person who shortens a text.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「删节者」，指删短文本的人。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning complete, with nothing removed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未删节的、完整的」。

entries.definition: To shorten a word or phrase, from the same Latin adjective brevis.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩写」，来自同一个拉丁形容词 brevis。

entries.definition: To make something less long in space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩短」，使某物在空间或时间上变短。

entries.definition: To make a text or substance denser by reducing it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「压缩、浓缩」，通过减少使文本或物质更密实。

entries.definition: To shorten a word, name, or text.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩写、缩短」，指缩短单词、名称或文本。

entries.definition: To cut short or reduce something, especially a right or plan.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩减、缩短」，尤指削减权利或计划。

entries.definition: To cut off the end of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「截断」，切掉某物的末端。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the publishing collocations and the shared Latin 'short'; the abstract hooks picture the thick book becoming thin.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用出版搭配与共享的拉丁语「短」；抽象记忆点想象厚书变薄。

normal.en: Abridged edition and abridged version are the standard publishing phrases.
normal.cn: abridged edition 与 abridged version 是标准出版短语。

normal.en: Unabridged means nothing was cut; it is the opposite of abridged.
normal.cn: unabridged 表示未删节，是 abridged 的反面。

normal.en: Abridge and abbreviate share Latin brevis, 'short'.
normal.cn: abridge 与 abbreviate 共享拉丁语 brevis（短）。

normal.en: The spellings abridgement and abridgment are both correct.
normal.cn: abridgement 与 abridgment 两种拼写都正确。

normal.en: Abridge rights is a legal warning phrase about cutting freedoms.
normal.cn: abridge rights 是关于削减自由的法律警告短语。

abstract.en: Picture a thick book squeezed under a press until it is a slim pamphlet.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书在压机下被压成薄薄的小册子。

abstract.en: Picture a tree pruned back to its trunk, with the side branches removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树被修回主干，侧枝全被剪掉。

abstract.en: Picture a long speech cut with scissors until only the key pages remain.
abstract.cn: 想象一篇长演讲被剪刀裁过，只剩关键几页。

examples.en: The novel was abridged for young readers.
examples.cn: 这部小说为年轻读者作了删节。

examples.en: No law may abridge the freedom of speech.
examples.cn: 任何法律都不得削减言论自由。

examples.en: We read an abridged translation of the play.
examples.cn: 我们读了这个剧本的节译本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额布里奇」——厚书像一座桥，删掉多余的桥段，只留能走人的主桥。

root: 晚期拉丁语 abbreviare（使变短），源自 brevis（短），经古法语 abregier 进入英语；核心义是「把长东西裁短」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from shortening books and speeches, through condensing and saving time, to legally cutting rights and privileges.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从删节书籍与演讲，经过压缩文本与节省时间，走到法律上削减权利与特权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick volume trimmed down to its trunk
core.cn: 核心意象：一本厚书被修裁到只剩主干

branches.en: Texts, speeches, and reports are shortened while their main content stays.
branches.cn: 文本、演讲与报告被缩短，同时保留主要内容。

branches.en: Rights and privileges are cut down, with legal consequences.
branches.cn: 权利与特权被削减，并带有法律后果。

branches.en: Time, distance, and felt duration are made shorter.
branches.cn: 时间、距离与感受中的时长被缩短。

branches.en: Condensation keeps the trunk and removes side growth.
branches.cn: 压缩保留主干，去掉侧枝。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem abbrevi-, reshaped in French to abreg-, with noun, adjective, and agent endings.

latinIntro.en: Latin brevis and abbreviare are the direct source of abridge and abbreviate, so the Latin entries record the adjective and the verb.

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「删节；节略本」
形容词，义为「删节过的；简略的」

definition_zh: 突然的；唐突的；陡峭的；生硬的
definition_en: happening suddenly and unexpectedly, or speaking and behaving in a blunt, unfriendly way
core_image: 一条绳子被猛地扯断，断口整齐而突然
scene: 话说到一半，他忽然站起来推门走了。His abrupt departure left the meeting in silence.
sceneCN: 这里 abrupt 是「突然的」（第 1 个义项：事情毫无预兆地发生）；句意为他突然离席，让会议陷入沉默。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「突然地；生硬地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「突然；唐突；陡峭」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「突然分离；断裂」

senses.title: Happening suddenly
senses.definition: happening quickly and without warning
senses.definitionCN: 迅速发生且毫无预兆
senses.example: The car came to an abrupt halt.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车骤然停下。
senses.why: Latin abrumpere meant 'to break off'; an abrupt event is one that snaps off the expected sequence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abrumpere 意为「折断」；abrupt 的事件就是从预期的序列上突然折断的事件。

senses.title: Blunt in speech
senses.definition: speaking in a short, blunt way that seems rude
senses.definitionCN: 说话简短生硬，显得无礼
senses.example: His abrupt reply surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他唐突的回答让所有人吃惊。
senses.why: Speech that breaks off instead of softening feels like a cut rope; the social surface is snapped.
senses.whyCN: 不铺垫而直接截断的话语像被剪断的绳子；社交表面被突然扯断。

senses.title: Steep in slope
senses.definition: rising or falling sharply, with little gradual slope
senses.definitionCN: 上升或下降很急，几乎没有缓坡
senses.example: The path ended at an abrupt cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 小路尽头是一道陡峭的悬崖。
senses.why: A cliff breaks the ground's smooth line, so the same word describes terrain that drops off without transition.
senses.whyCN: 悬崖打断地面的平滑线条，因此同一个词也描述毫无过渡就下落的地形。

senses.title: Cut off in a text
senses.definition: of a story, sentence, or ending, stopping without preparation
senses.definitionCN: 指故事、句子或结尾毫无铺垫地停止
senses.example: The novel has an abrupt ending.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的结尾很突然。
senses.why: A text that stops mid-thought reproduces the broken edge: the reader feels the snap.
senses.whyCN: 思路中途停止的文本重现了那个断口：读者能感到那一下折断。

senses.title: Rough in manner
senses.definition: behaving in a way that lacks warmth or courtesy
senses.definitionCN: 举止缺少温度或礼貌
senses.example: She was abrupt with the new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 她对新员工态度生硬。
senses.why: Social behaviour can also snap short; warmth is removed as abruptly as a severed line.
senses.whyCN: 社交行为也能突然截短；温度被拿掉，就像一根线被突然剪断。

senses.title: Sharp in change
senses.definition: changing by a large amount in a short time
senses.definitionCN: 在短时间内发生大幅变化
senses.example: There was an abrupt rise in prices.
senses.exampleCN: 价格急剧上涨。
senses.why: A graph line that turns almost vertically marks a break in the trend, and the word follows it.
senses.whyCN: 折线几乎垂直转向，标记趋势的中断，这个词也跟着这条线走。

senses.title: Sudden in transition
senses.definition: moving from one subject or state to another without transition
senses.definitionCN: 从一个主题或状态毫无过渡地转到另一个
senses.example: The conversation took an abrupt turn.
senses.exampleCN: 谈话突然转了向。
senses.why: Transition is a bridge; an abrupt turn removes the bridge and leaves a gap.
senses.whyCN: 过渡是一座桥；abrupt 的转折拆掉这座桥，留下一个断口。

senses.title: Stopping without easing
senses.definition: ending an action without slowing down or preparing
senses.definitionCN: 结束动作时不减速、不铺垫
senses.example: The music stopped abruptly.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐戛然而止。
senses.why: The core image of a snap without a slowdown is clearest when a sound or motion simply ceases.
senses.whyCN: 「不减速直接折断」的核心意象，在声音或运动干脆停止时最为清楚。

intro.en: Abrupt comes from a Latin participle meaning 'broken off', built from a prefix and the verb for breaking.
intro.cn: abrupt 来自一个意为「被折断的」拉丁语分词，由前缀与表示「折断」的动词构成。

items.en: The root *reup- is reconstructed with the sense 'to snatch, break'; it also lies behind rupture.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *reup- 被重构为「抓、折断」之义；rupture 也源自它。

items.en: rumpere meant 'to break, burst', and it produced rupture, erupt, and interrupt.
items.cn: rumpere 意为「折断、爆裂」，衍生出 rupture、erupt、interrupt。

items.en: ab- 'away' plus rumpere formed abrumpere, 'to break off'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 rumpere 构成 abrumpere，意为「折断、使分离」。

items.en: The past participle abruptus, 'broken off', is the direct source of the adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词 abruptus 意为「被折断的」，是形容词的直接来源。

items.en: English adopted abrupt first for steep terrain and then for sudden events and manner.
items.cn: 英语先吸收 abrupt 表示陡峭地形，随后用于突然事件与态度。

items.en: The social sense 'blunt, curt' became common, and the word now covers changes, endings, and behaviour.
items.cn: 「生硬、唐突」的社交义变得常见，如今这个词覆盖变化、结尾与举止。

note.en: The first group gathers adverb, noun, and same-root words; the second gathers adjectives for suddenness, bluntness, and steepness.
note.cn: 第一组收副词、名词与同根词；第二组收表示突然、生硬与陡峭的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'suddenly or bluntly'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「突然地」或「生硬地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being sudden, blunt, or steep.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「突然、唐突、陡峭」。

entries.definition: A sudden breaking off or separation, used especially in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「突然分离、断裂」，尤用于医学。

entries.definition: A break or burst, from the same Latin verb rumpere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「破裂、断裂」，来自同一个拉丁动词 rumpere。

entries.definition: To break into a conversation or process, from the same breaking verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打断」，来自同一个表示折断的动词。

entries.definition: Happening quickly and without warning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「突然的」，迅速发生且没有预兆。

entries.definition: Short and rude in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「简短无礼的」，说话短促而失礼。

entries.definition: Direct to the point of being rude.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「直率的、生硬的」，直接到近乎无礼。

entries.definition: Rising or falling at a sharp angle.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「陡峭的」，以很急的角度上升或下降。

entries.definition: Done quickly, often too quickly to be careful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「仓促的」，做得很快，常快到不够谨慎。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin breaking image and the common collocations; the abstract hooks picture the snap itself.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「折断」意象与常见搭配；抽象记忆点想象折断的瞬间。

normal.en: Abrupt and rupture share Latin rumpere, 'to break'.
normal.cn: abrupt 与 rupture 共享拉丁语 rumpere（折断）。

normal.en: An abrupt change, an abrupt end, and an abrupt manner are standard collocations.
normal.cn: an abrupt change、an abrupt end、an abrupt manner 都是标准搭配。

normal.en: The adverb is abruptly, as in 'the music stopped abruptly'.
normal.cn: 副词是 abruptly，如「音乐戛然而止」。

normal.en: The abstract noun abruptness names the quality; abruption is the medical break.
normal.cn: 抽象名词 abruptness 指这种性质；abruption 是医学上的「突然分离」。

normal.en: The same adjective covers a steep cliff and a blunt reply.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词既形容陡崖，也形容生硬的回答。

abstract.en: Picture a taut rope snapping with a clean, sharp edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绷紧的绳子啪地折断，断口干净利落。

abstract.en: Picture a graph line that turns straight down instead of curving.
abstract.cn: 想象折线没有转弯过渡，而是直直下坠。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that stops in the middle, leaving the page blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话停在中间，纸面留下空白。

examples.en: The meeting came to an abrupt end.
examples.cn: 会议突然结束了。

examples.en: He was abrupt with the reporters.
examples.cn: 他对记者态度生硬。

examples.en: An abrupt change in wind direction caught the sailors.
examples.cn: 风向的突然变化让水手们措手不及。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额布拉普特」——绳子绷得太紧，啪一声断掉，事情也就突然停住。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ rumpere（折断），过去分词 abruptus（被折断的）；核心义是「像断绳一样突然断开」

sensesIntro.en: The senses all grow from a clean break: events snap, speech snaps, slopes snap downward, and stories snap off.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都从「干净利落的折断」生长出来：事件突然断开、话语突然截断、坡面突然下落、故事突然中止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope breaking with a sharp, clean edge
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子带着干净断口骤然折断

branches.en: Events, changes, and movements stop or shift without warning.
branches.cn: 事件、变化与运动毫无预警地停止或转向。

branches.en: Speech and manner break off instead of softening.
branches.cn: 言语与举止直接截断，而不作缓和。

branches.en: Terrain drops in a sharp edge rather than a gentle curve.
branches.cn: 地形以锐利边缘下落，而非平缓曲线。

branches.en: A text or story stops without preparation.
branches.cn: 文本或故事毫无铺垫地停止。

branches.en: A transition removes its bridge and leaves a gap.
branches.cn: 转折拆掉过渡的桥，留下断口。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem abrupt-, the adjective ending itself, and the adverb and noun endings -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 abrupt-、形容词词尾本身，以及副词与名词后缀 -ly、-ness 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin abrumpere and abruptus are the direct source of abrupt, so the Latin entries record the verb and its participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abrumpere 与 abruptus 是 abrupt 的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其分词。
