名词，义为「突然；唐突；陡峭」

definition_zh: 脱落；（植物器官的）自然脱落；切除
definition_en: the natural shedding of a plant part such as a leaf or fruit, or the act of cutting something off
core_image: 一片叶子在叶柄基部被一层细胞轻轻断开，随风落下
scene: 秋天一到，树叶基部形成一层特殊细胞，让叶片自然落下。Leaf abscission begins when the days grow shorter.
sceneCN: 这里 abscission 是「（植物器官的）自然脱落」（第 1 个义项：植物主动断开并舍弃某部分）；句意为白昼变短时，叶片脱落开始。

pos.zh: 脱落；（植物）器官自然脱落

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀构成，义为「脱落；切断」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「脱落酸的；与脱落有关的」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「脱落素」，脱落酸的旧称

senses.title: Shedding of plant parts
senses.definition: the natural dropping of leaves, fruits, flowers, or other plant parts
senses.definitionCN: 叶片、果实、花或其他植物部位的自然掉落
senses.example: Leaf abscission is controlled by plant hormones.
senses.exampleCN: 叶片脱落受植物激素控制。
senses.why: Latin abscindere meant 'to cut off'; the plant cuts its own leaf, and the word names that controlled separation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abscindere 意为「切掉」；植物自己把叶子切断，这个词命名了这种受控的分离。

senses.title: The fall of leaves
senses.definition: the seasonal process by which leaves are shed from a tree
senses.definitionCN: 树木按季节把叶子舍弃的过程
senses.example: Autumn abscission removes water‑losing leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 秋季脱落会去掉会失水的叶子。
senses.why: Seasonal leaf fall is the most visible case of the plant cutting away a whole organ before winter.
senses.whyCN: 季节性落叶是植物在入冬前切掉整个器官最显眼的例子。

senses.title: The drop of fruit
senses.definition: the shedding of fruit before or after ripening
senses.definitionCN: 果实在成熟前后掉落
senses.example: Premature fruit abscission reduces the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 果实过早脱落会减少收成。
senses.why: Fruit is cut free at the stalk when the plant no longer supports it, so the same separation image applies.
senses.whyCN: 当植物不再供养果实时，果实就在果柄处被切离，因此同一个分离意象适用。

senses.title: Surgical removal
senses.definition: the removal of a part by cutting, especially in older medical writing
senses.definitionCN: 通过切割去除某部分，尤见于较早医学文献
senses.example: The older term abscission referred to cutting away tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的术语 abscission 指把组织切掉。
senses.why: Medicine used the literal sense first: tissue is cut off, exactly as the Latin verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 医学先使用这个字面义：组织被切掉，正如拉丁动词所描述的那样。

senses.title: The abscission zone
senses.definition: the layer of cells at the base of a plant part where separation occurs
senses.definitionCN: 植物器官基部发生分离的细胞层
senses.example: A visible line marks the abscission zone.
senses.exampleCN: 一条可见的线标出脱落区。
senses.why: The zone is the seam where the cut will happen, so the place of separation takes the name of the process.
senses.whyCN: 脱落区就是即将发生切断的接缝，于是分离的地点借用了过程的名字。

senses.title: Separation of flowers
senses.definition: the shedding of petals or whole flowers after pollination
senses.definitionCN: 授粉后花瓣或整朵花的掉落
senses.example: Flower abscission follows pollination in many species.
senses.exampleCN: 许多物种在授粉后发生花器官脱落。
senses.why: Once pollination is done, the flower's work is finished, and the plant cuts the now-useless parts away.
senses.whyCN: 授粉完成后，花的任务就结束了，植物便把不再有用的部分切掉。

senses.title: Cutting off in general
senses.definition: the act of cutting something away from its base
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从基部切离的行为
senses.example: The word abscission is rare outside botany and surgery.
senses.exampleCN: abscission 一词在植物学与外科之外很少使用。
senses.why: The general sense is simply the Latin verb translated: any cutting away from a base.
senses.whyCN: 一般义就是拉丁动词的直译：任何从基部切离的行为。

senses.title: A sharp separation
senses.definition: a sudden or clean separation of one thing from another
senses.definitionCN: 一物从另一物上突然或干净地分离
senses.example: The report describes the abscission of the ice shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了冰架的断裂分离。
senses.why: Large structures can also break along a seam, so the botanical image extends to ice and rock.
senses.whyCN: 大型结构也能沿接缝断开，因此植物学意象延伸到冰体与岩石。

intro.en: Abscission comes from a Latin noun for cutting off, built from a prefix and the verb for cutting.
intro.cn: abscission 来自一个意为「切掉」的拉丁语名词，由前缀与表示「切」的动词构成。

items.en: The root *skheID- is reconstructed with the sense 'to cut, split'; the exact reconstruction varies among sources.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *skheID- 被重构为「切、劈」之义；不同来源的具体重构形式不一致。

items.en: scindere meant 'to cut, split', and it also lies behind scissors and rescind.
items.cn: scindere 意为「切、劈」，scissors 与 rescind 也源自它。

items.en: ab- 'away' plus scindere formed abscindere, 'to cut off'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 scindere 构成 abscindere，意为「切掉」。

items.en: The noun abscissio named the act of cutting off, the direct source of English abscission.
items.cn: 名词 abscissio 指切掉的行为，是英语 abscission 的直接来源。

items.en: English abscission first appeared in medical and general writing for cutting away a part.
items.cn: 英语 abscission 最初出现在医学与一般文献中，指切去某部分。

items.en: Botany made the word central for the natural shedding of leaves and fruit, especially through the abscission zone.
items.cn: 植物学使这个词成为叶果自然脱落的核心术语，尤其通过「脱落区」的概念。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, the acid adjective, and two other cutting words; the second gathers nouns for natural shedding and removal.
note.cn: 第一组收动词、酸的形容词与另外两个「切」词；第二组收表示自然脱落与去除的名词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to cut off or to be shed naturally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「切掉」或「自然脱落」。

entries.definition: An adjective used in abscisic acid, the hormone that controls shedding.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，用于 abscisic acid（脱落酸），即控制脱落的激素。

entries.definition: The horizontal coordinate in mathematics, literally 'a cut-off line'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「横坐标」，字面是「被切下的一段线」。

entries.definition: A cutting tool, from the same Latin verb scindere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「剪刀」，来自同一个拉丁动词 scindere。

entries.definition: To cancel a law or agreement, literally to cut it away.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「废除、取消」，字面是「把它切掉」。

entries.definition: The natural dropping of leaves, skin, or hair.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脱落」，指叶、皮或毛发的自然掉落。

entries.definition: The state of becoming separate from something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分离、脱离」，指与某物分开的状态。

entries.definition: The act of taking something away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「去除、移除」，指把某物拿走的动作。

entries.definition: The surgical cutting out of a part.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「切除」，指外科切去某部分。

entries.definition: The act of dividing or coming apart.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分离」，指分开或断离的行为。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the botanical collocations and the shared Latin cutting root; the abstract hooks picture the leaf's clean break.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用植物学搭配与共享的拉丁「切」词根；抽象记忆点想象叶片干净的断口。

normal.en: Leaf abscission and abscission zone are the core botanical phrases.
normal.cn: leaf abscission 与 abscission zone 是核心植物学短语。

normal.en: Abscisic acid is the hormone named after abscission.
normal.cn: abscisic acid（脱落酸）是以 abscission 命名的激素。

normal.en: Abscission and scissors share Latin scindere, 'to cut'.
normal.cn: abscission 与 scissors 共享拉丁语 scindere（切）。

normal.en: The verb is abscise, and the adjective abscisic belongs to the acid.
normal.cn: 动词是 abscise，形容词 abscisic 属于那种酸。

normal.en: In older medicine abscission meant cutting away tissue.
normal.cn: 在较早的医学中，abscission 指切去组织。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf stem developing a thin line of cells, then letting go.
abstract.cn: 想象叶柄长出一条薄薄的细胞线，然后松手。

abstract.en: Picture a fruit dropping onto grass while the branch stays intact.
abstract.cn: 想象果实落到草地上，而树枝完好无损。

abstract.en: Picture an ice shelf cracking along a clean seam and sliding away.
abstract.cn: 想象冰架沿一条干净的接缝裂开并滑走。

examples.en: Abscission protects trees from losing too much water.
examples.cn: 脱落能保护树木不过度失水。

examples.en: The abscission zone forms at the base of the leaf.
examples.cn: 脱落区在叶片基部形成。

examples.en: Fruit abscission can be triggered by stress.
examples.cn: 果实脱落可能由胁迫引发。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布西申」——叶子基部像被小剪刀轻轻一剪，叶子就脱离枝条落下来。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ scindere（切），构成 abscindere（切掉），名词 abscissio；核心义是「沿一条线干净地切离」

sensesIntro.en: The senses center on the plant's controlled cutting away of leaves, fruit, and flowers, with extensions to surgery and clean separation.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项围绕植物受控地切离叶片、果实与花，并延伸到外科切除与干净分离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leaf cut free along a thin seam of cells
core.cn: 核心意象：叶片沿一条薄细胞缝被切离

branches.en: Plant parts are shed in a controlled seasonal process.
branches.cn: 植物部位在受控的季节过程中脱落。

branches.en: The abscission zone is the anatomical seam where separation happens.
branches.cn: 脱落区是发生分离的解剖接缝。

branches.en: Older medicine used the word for cutting tissue away.
branches.cn: 较早的医学用这个词表示切去组织。

branches.en: The general sense is any cutting away from a base.
branches.cn: 一般义是从基部切离任何东西。

branches.en: Clean separation extends to ice shelves and other structures.
branches.cn: 干净分离延伸到冰架及其他结构。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem absciss-, the prefix ab-, and the endings -ion, -ize, and -ic.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 absciss-、前缀 ab-，以及后缀 -ion、-ize、-ic 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin abscindere and abscissio are the direct source of abscission, so the Latin entries record the verb and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abscindere 与 abscissio 是 abscission 的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其名词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「脱落；切断」
形容词，义为「脱落酸的；与脱落有关的」

definition_zh: 缺席的；不在的；缺乏的；心不在焉的
definition_en: not present in a place, not existing, or showing that one's mind is elsewhere
core_image: 点名册上的名字还在，座位却空着
scene: 点名时老师念到一个名字，座位却仍然空着。One student was absent from class again.
sceneCN: 这里 absent 是「缺席的」（第 1 个义项：该在场的人不在场）；句意为又有一名学生没来上课。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「缺席；缺乏」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「心不在焉地」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「缺席者；旷工者」
由 absentee 加表示现象的后缀构成，义为「旷工；缺勤」

senses.title: Not present at a place
senses.definition: not present in a particular place at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 在特定时间不在特定场所
senses.example: Three students were absent from class.
senses.exampleCN: 有三名学生没来上课。
senses.why: Latin absens is the present participle of abesse, 'to be away'; the person is simply not at the expected place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absens 是 abesse（不在、离开）的现在分词；这个人只是不在应在的地方。

senses.title: Not existing
senses.definition: not existing or not available in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在某种情况下不存在或不可得
senses.example: Confidence was absent from his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他的声音里没有自信。
senses.why: What is 'away' can also be simply missing, so the word moves from people to qualities that are not there.
senses.whyCN: 「离开」的东西也可以只是「没有」，于是这个词从人扩展到并不存在的性质。

senses.title: Distracted in mind
senses.definition: showing that one's attention is somewhere else
senses.definitionCN: 表现出注意力在别处
senses.example: She gave an absent nod.
senses.exampleCN: 她心不在焉地点了点头。
senses.why: A mind that has left the room is pictured as a person who is away, so absent describes the inner departure.
senses.whyCN: 心思离开房间被想象成人不在场，因此 absent 描述的是内在的离开。

senses.title: Recorded as not at work
senses.definition: officially not at work or school, often with a recorded reason
senses.definitionCN: 正式地不在工作或学校，常记录原因
senses.example: He was absent from work for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他缺勤了一周。
senses.why: Employers and schools turn the plain fact of absence into a record, and the adjective follows the entry.
senses.whyCN: 雇主与学校把「不在」这一事实变成记录，形容词也跟着记录走。

senses.title: Missing from a text or list
senses.definition: not included where it should appear
senses.definitionCN: 本应出现却没有被列入
senses.example: The word is absent from the index.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词在索引里没有出现。
senses.why: A list is a place where items are expected to be present; an item that is not there is absent from it.
senses.whyCN: 清单是期待条目出现的地方；不在那里的条目就是 absent from 它。

senses.title: Legally not in court
senses.definition: not present in court, especially in a trial held in one's absence
senses.definitionCN: 未出庭，尤指在当事人不在场时进行的审判
senses.example: The defendant was tried in absentia.
senses.exampleCN: 被告在缺席的情况下受审。
senses.why: Law uses the plain physical sense: the accused is not in the courtroom, and proceedings continue without them.
senses.whyCN: 法律使用朴素的物理义：被告不在法庭，程序在他们不在场的情况下继续。

senses.title: A vacant expression
senses.definition: describing eyes or a face that seem to look at nothing
senses.definitionCN: 形容目光或表情似乎没有焦点
senses.example: He stared at the page with an absent expression.
senses.exampleCN: 他茫然地盯着书页。
senses.why: The face registers the mind's departure: attention is away, and the expression empties.
senses.whyCN: 面容显示出心思的离开：注意力不在，表情就空了。

senses.title: Away without permission
senses.definition: not at one's post without official leave
senses.definitionCN: 未获正式准假而不在岗位
senses.example: The soldier was absent without leave.
senses.exampleCN: 那名士兵擅离职守。
senses.why: The military phrase makes absence a disciplinary matter, with the adjective marking the missing person.
senses.whyCN: 军事短语把缺席变成纪律问题，形容词标记那个不在的人。

intro.en: Absent comes from the Latin verb 'to be away', built from a prefix and the verb 'to be'.
intro.cn: absent 来自拉丁语动词「不在、离开」，由前缀与动词「是、在」构成。

items.en: esse meant 'to be', and it is the source of essence, essential, and present.
items.cn: esse 意为「是、存在」，是 essence、essential 与 present 的来源。

items.en: ab is the preposition 'from, away from'.
items.cn: ab 是介词，意为「从、离开」。

items.en: ab- plus esse formed abesse, 'to be away or absent'.
items.cn: ab- 与 esse 构成 abesse，意为「不在、离开」。

items.en: The present participle absens, 'being away', is the direct model of English absent.
items.cn: 现在分词 absens 意为「不在的」，是英语 absent 的直接模型。

items.en: Old French absent carried the adjective into medieval use.
items.cn: 古法语 absent 把这个形容词带入中世纪用法。

items.cn: 英语把 absent 从物理上的不在，扩展到缺失的性质与走神的心智。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adverb, and person forms from the same family; the second gathers adjectives for not being there.

entries.definition: The noun meaning the state of being away or the lack of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席」或「缺乏」，指不在的状态或某物的缺失。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in a distracted way'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「心不在焉地」。

entries.definition: A person who is not present, especially one who often stays away from work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席者、旷工者」，尤指经常不上班的人。

entries.definition: Being in the place mentioned; the opposite of absent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「在场的」，是 absent 的反面，同样来自拉丁语 esse。

entries.definition: Not present where expected, and often unaccounted for.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「缺失的、失踪的」，不在应在之处，常下落不明。

entries.definition: Not at the usual place, often for a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「不在的、外出的」，常指离开一段时间。

entries.definition: Forgetful or distracted because one's attention is elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「心不在焉的、健忘的」，因注意力在别处而走神。

entries.definition: Not able to be reached or used at a particular time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无法获得的、联系不上的」。

entries.definition: No longer present or no longer existing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不在的、消失的」，不再存在或不在场。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the fixed 'absent from' pattern and the school and military phrases; the abstract hooks picture the empty seat.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用固定结构 absent from 与学校、军队短语；抽象记忆点想象空座位。

normal.en: Absent from is the standard pattern: absent from class, absent from work.
normal.cn: absent from 是标准结构：absent from class、absent from work。

normal.en: Absent without leave is the military phrase for being away without permission.
normal.cn: absent without leave 是军事短语，表示未经许可缺席。

normal.en: An absent look or an absent nod shows a mind that has gone elsewhere.
normal.cn: an absent look 或 an absent nod 表示心思已飘到别处。

normal.en: Absence is the noun, and absent is the adjective, both from Latin abesse.
normal.cn: 名词是 absence，形容词是 absent，二者都来自拉丁语 abesse。

normal.en: Present is the opposite, and it shares the same Latin verb esse.
normal.cn: 反义词 present 共享同一个拉丁动词 esse。

abstract.en: Picture a name still written on the roll while the chair stays empty.
abstract.cn: 想象点名册上名字还在，椅子却空着。

abstract.en: Picture eyes looking at a page but focused on nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象眼睛看着书页，却没有聚焦在任何东西上。

abstract.en: Picture a coat hook with no coat, marking someone's departure.
abstract.cn: 想象衣钩上没挂外套，标示着某人已经离开。

examples.en: She was absent from school for two days.
examples.cn: 她两天没去上学。

examples.en: The ingredient is absent from the label.
examples.cn: 标签上缺少这种成分。

examples.en: His absent manner made it hard to talk to him.
examples.cn: 他心不在焉的样子让人很难交谈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布森特」——点名时名字还在，座位上却没有人，那就是缺席。

sensesIntro.en: The senses grow from physical absence to missing qualities, a distracted mind, recorded absence, legal absence, and absence without permission.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从物理上的不在，扩展到缺失的性质、走神的心智、记录的缺勤、法律缺席与未经许可的缺席。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair beside a name on the roll
core.cn: 核心意象：点名册名字旁的一把空椅子

branches.en: A person is not where they are expected to be, often recorded.
branches.cn: 人不在应在之处，且常被记录。

branches.en: A quality or item is not present, so something is lacking.
branches.cn: 某种性质或条目不在，因而有所缺失。

branches.en: The mind has left, and the face or gesture shows it.
branches.cn: 心思离开，面容或动作显示出来。

branches.en: The law proceeds even when the accused is not in court.
branches.cn: 即使被告不在法庭，法律程序仍继续。

branches.en: Absence without permission becomes a disciplinary offence.
branches.cn: 未经许可的缺席成为纪律过失。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem absent-, the noun ending -ence, and the person and phenomenon endings -ee and -ism.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 absent-、名词后缀 -ence，以及表示人物与现象的后缀 -ee、-ism 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin abesse and absens are the direct source of absent, so the Latin entries record the verb and its participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abesse 与 absens 是 absent 的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其分词。

definition_zh: 旷工；缺勤；长期缺席的现象
definition_en: the habit or pattern of frequently being absent from work, school, or another duty
core_image: 一排工位上总有几个空位，天天如此
scene: 工厂主管翻看月度记录，发现请病假的人越来越多。High absenteeism was slowing production at the plant.
sceneCN: 这里 absenteeism 是「旷工、缺勤现象」（第 1 个义项：员工经常不到岗的整体模式）；句意为高缺勤率正在拖慢工厂生产。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉表示现象的后缀构成，义为「缺席者；旷工者」
由本词去掉后缀构成，义为「缺席的；不在的」
由本词去掉后缀构成，义为「缺席；缺乏」

senses.title: Habitual absence from work
senses.definition: the pattern of workers regularly failing to come to work
senses.definitionCN: 员工经常不到岗的整体模式
senses.example: High absenteeism was slowing production.
senses.exampleCN: 高缺勤率正在拖慢生产。
senses.why: Absenteeism adds -ism to absentee, turning a person who is away into a collective social pattern.
senses.whyCN: absenteeism 在 absentee 后加 -ism，把「不在的人」变成一种集体的社会现象。

senses.title: Pupil absenteeism
senses.definition: the rate at which students miss school
senses.definitionCN: 学生缺课的比例或模式
senses.example: The school reported rising absenteeism in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 学校报告冬季缺课现象上升。
senses.why: The same pattern word applies to schools, where missing class is measured as a rate.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「模式」的词适用于学校，缺课在那里被当作比率衡量。

senses.title: Unexcused absence
senses.definition: absence without a valid reason, considered as a problem
senses.definitionCN: 没有正当理由的缺席，被视为问题
senses.example: The policy targets unexcused absenteeism.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策针对无正当理由的缺勤。
senses.why: The -ism suffix turns repeated unexcused absence into a recognized category for managers.
senses.whyCN: -ism 后缀把反复的无故缺席变成管理者认可的一类问题。

senses.title: Long-term absence
senses.definition: absence that continues over an extended period
senses.definitionCN: 持续较长时间的缺席
senses.example: Long-term absenteeism often follows a serious illness.
senses.exampleCN: 长期缺勤常常出现在重病之后。
senses.why: When absence lasts long enough to become a state rather than an event, the abstract noun fits.
senses.whyCN: 当缺席长到成为状态而非事件时，这个抽象名词就适用了。

senses.title: Sickness absence
senses.definition: absence attributed to illness, tracked by employers
senses.definitionCN: 归因于疾病的缺勤，由雇主统计
senses.example: Sickness absenteeism rose during the flu season.
senses.exampleCN: 流感季期间因病缺勤上升。
senses.why: Health reasons are the most common source of the pattern, so the word often appears with sickness.
senses.whyCN: 健康原因是最常见的模式来源，因此这个词常与 sickness 连用。

senses.title: An organisational problem
senses.definition: the overall level of absence treated as a management issue
senses.definitionCN: 被当作管理问题处理的整体缺席水平
senses.example: The report links absenteeism to low morale.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把缺勤与士气低落联系起来。
senses.why: Once absence is measured across a workforce, it becomes an indicator of how an organisation is doing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦在整个劳动力范围内衡量缺席，它就成为组织运行状况的指标。

senses.title: Landlord absenteeism
senses.definition: the historical pattern of owners living away from their estates
senses.definitionCN: 历史上地主不住在自己的地产上、长期不在地的现象
senses.example: The old estate suffered from landlord absenteeism.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧庄园深受不在地主现象之苦。
senses.why: The word once described owners who were absent from their land, an older sense now overshadowed by workplace use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾描述不在自己土地上的所有者，这个较早义如今被职场用法盖过。

senses.title: Absence from meetings
senses.definition: the pattern of members regularly missing meetings
senses.definitionCN: 成员经常不参加会议的模式
senses.example: Committee absenteeism delayed every vote.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会成员的缺席让每次表决都推迟。
senses.why: Any group that expects attendance can turn repeated absence into the same -ism pattern.
senses.whyCN: 任何期待出席的群体，都能把反复缺席变成同样的 -ism 现象。

intro.en: Absenteeism is a modern formation: the person noun absentee plus the suffix -ism for a practice or pattern.
intro.cn: absenteeism 是现代构词：人物名词 absentee 加表示做法或模式的后缀 -ism。

items.en: abesse meant 'to be away', from ab- 'away' and esse 'to be'.
items.cn: abesse 意为「不在、离开」，由 ab-（离开）与 esse（存在）构成。

items.en: The participle absens, 'being away', produced English absent.
items.cn: 分词 absens 意为「不在的」，构成英语 absent。

items.en: English absentee, formed with the person suffix -ee, named someone who lives away from their property or duty.
items.cn: 英语 absentee 由人物后缀 -ee 构成，指不住在自己的产业或岗位所在地的人。

items.en: The suffix -ism turns a person or practice into a named system or pattern.
items.cn: 后缀 -ism 把人物或做法变成被命名的制度或模式。

items.en: Absenteeism appeared in the nineteenth century, first often in reports about landlords who lived away from their estates.
items.cn: absenteeism 出现在十九世纪，最初常见于关于不在地主的报告。

items.en: Modern usage shifted the centre of gravity to workplaces and schools, where absenteeism is measured as a rate.
items.cn: 现代用法把重心转到职场与学校，缺勤在那里被当作比率衡量。

note.en: The first group gathers the person, adjective, and noun from which the word is built; the second gathers words for absence and skipping.
note.cn: 第一组收构成本词的人物、形容词与名词；第二组收表示缺席与逃避的词。

entries.definition: A person who is regularly away from work or property.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席者、旷工者」，指经常不在工作或产业所在地的人。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning not present.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「缺席的、不在的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席、不在」，指离开的状态。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in a distracted manner'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「心不在焉地」。

entries.definition: A single period of being away, rather than a repeated pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席」，指一次离开的时段，而非反复的模式。

entries.definition: The practice of staying away from school without permission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「逃学」，指未经允许不去上学的做法。

entries.definition: The fact of not being present at an event or institution.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「未出席、未到场」。

entries.definition: The informal British word for avoiding work or duty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式非正式用语，义为「偷懒、逃避工作」。

entries.definition: A person who fails to appear when expected.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爽约者、未到场者」，指应出现却没出现的人。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks build the word from absentee plus -ism and connect it to workplace metrics; the abstract hooks picture the row of empty desks.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点把词拆成 absentee 加 -ism，并联系职场指标；抽象记忆点想象一排空工位。

normal.en: Absentee plus -ism: the person who is away becomes the pattern of being away.
normal.cn: absentee 加 -ism：不在的人变成了「不在」的整体模式。

normal.en: Reduce absenteeism and absenteeism rates are standard management phrases.
normal.cn: reduce absenteeism 与 absenteeism rates 是标准管理短语。

normal.en: Sickness absenteeism separates health-related absence from other kinds.
normal.cn: sickness absenteeism 把与健康相关的缺勤与其他缺勤区分开。

normal.en: Chronic absenteeism describes a long-running pattern rather than one missed day.
normal.cn: chronic absenteeism 描述长期模式，而不是某一天没来。

normal.en: The word began with landlords who lived away from their estates.
normal.cn: 这个词最初指不住在自己庄园的地主。

abstract.en: Picture a row of desks with three chairs empty every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一排工位，每天早上都有三把椅子空着。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with the same dates crossed out month after month.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上同样的日期被一月月地划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a manager's chart with a line that refuses to fall.
abstract.cn: 想象主管的图表上有一条怎么也不下降的线。

examples.en: The company introduced new rules to reduce absenteeism.
examples.cn: 公司出台新规以减少旷工。

examples.en: Absenteeism among night-shift staff remains high.
examples.cn: 夜班员工的缺勤率仍然很高。

examples.en: Chronic absenteeism affects a child's learning.
examples.cn: 长期缺课会影响孩子的学习。

core.cn: 核心意象：一排总是空着一半的工位

branches.cn: 工作中的反复缺席成为被认可的模式或问题。

branches.en: Schools and committees measure absence as a rate.
branches.cn: 学校与委员会把缺席当作比率衡量。

branches.en: Illness is the most common labelled cause of the pattern.

definition_en: complete and total, not limited by anything else, or holding unlimited power
core_image: 一个没有刻度、没有上限的满分表盘
scene: 山谷里连风声都停了，只剩下雪地的寂静。The hut stood in absolute silence at the top of the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 absolute 是「完全的、彻底的」（第 1 个义项：毫无混杂、达到极致）；句意为小屋立在绝对寂静的山谷顶端。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「绝对地；完全地」

senses.title: Complete and total
senses.definition: existing in the highest degree, with nothing mixed in or missing
senses.definitionCN: 达到最高程度，没有任何混杂或缺失
senses.example: The room was in absolute silence.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里一片绝对的寂静。
senses.why: Latin absolutus meant 'loosened, set free, completed'; something absolute is finished and free of every qualifying limit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absolutus 意为「被松开、被释放、已完成」；绝对之物已经完成，摆脱了一切限定。

senses.title: Unlimited in power
senses.definition: holding power that no other body can limit
senses.definitionCN: 掌握没有任何其他机构能够限制的权力
senses.example: The king ruled with absolute power.
senses.exampleCN: 国王以绝对权力统治。
senses.why: Power that is 'loosened' from all checks is unlimited, and the word becomes a political warning.
senses.whyCN: 摆脱一切制约的权力就是无限的，于是这个词带上政治警告。

senses.title: Certain beyond doubt
senses.definition: so certain that no doubt or condition can be attached
senses.definitionCN: 确定到无法附加任何怀疑或条件
senses.example: There is absolute proof of his innocence.
senses.exampleCN: 有确凿的证据证明他无罪。
senses.why: A proof released from every 'perhaps' is absolute; nothing can qualify it.
senses.whyCN: 从所有「也许」中释放出来的证据就是绝对的；任何东西都无法限定它。

senses.title: Unconditional
senses.definition: not dependent on any condition or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 不依赖任何条件或协议
senses.example: The offer was an absolute promise, not a conditional one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个提议是无条件的承诺，而非附条件的。
senses.why: The 'freed from limits' sense applies to promises: an absolute promise carries no ifs.
senses.whyCN: 「摆脱限制」的义适用于承诺：绝对的承诺不带任何「如果」。

senses.title: Out-and-out
senses.definition: used to stress that someone or something is completely the type described
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调某人或某物完全是所描述的类型
senses.example: He is an absolute beginner at chess.
senses.exampleCN: 他在国际象棋上完全是个新手。
senses.why: The intensifying use comes from the same completeness: no part of the person is anything else.
senses.whyCN: 强调用法来自同样的「完整」：这个人没有任何部分属于别的类型。

senses.title: Legally unconditional
senses.definition: describing a right or title that is not limited by conditions
senses.definitionCN: 形容不受条件限制的权利或所有权
senses.example: She holds an absolute right to the land.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这块土地拥有绝对权利。
senses.why: Law separates absolute rights from conditional ones, keeping the Latin idea of release from limits.
senses.whyCN: 法律把绝对权利与附条件权利分开，保留了拉丁语「摆脱限制」的观念。

senses.title: A fixed scientific value
senses.definition: describing a value fixed independently of changing conditions, as in absolute zero
senses.definitionCN: 形容不随条件变化的固定值，如绝对零度
senses.example: Absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 绝对零度是可能达到的最低温度。
senses.why: Science uses absolute for scales that do not depend on a chosen reference point.
senses.whyCN: 科学用 absolute 表示不依赖选定参照点的标度。

senses.title: Grammatically independent
senses.definition: describing a phrase that is grammatically independent of the rest of the sentence
senses.definitionCN: 形容在语法上独立于句子其余部分的短语
senses.example: The absolute construction stands apart from the main clause.
senses.exampleCN: 绝对结构独立于主句之外。
senses.why: Grammar borrows the word for a phrase 'loosened' from the sentence's main structure.
senses.whyCN: 语法借这个词指从句子主干结构上「松开」的短语。

intro.en: Absolute comes from a Latin participle meaning 'loosened, completed', built from a prefix and the verb for loosening.
intro.cn: absolute 来自一个意为「松开、完成」的拉丁语分词，由前缀与表示「松开」的动词构成。

items.en: solvere meant 'to loosen, dissolve, pay'; it produced solve, dissolve, and solution.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、溶解、支付」，衍生出 solve、dissolve、solution。

items.en: ab- 'away' plus solvere formed absolvere, 'to loosen from, set free, finish'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 solvere 构成 absolvere，意为「松开、释放、完成」。

items.en: The past participle absolutus meant 'completed, unconditional, freed from limits'.
items.cn: 过去分词 absolutus 意为「完成的、无条件的、摆脱限制的」。

items.en: The noun absolutio named a setting free or a completion.
items.cn: 名词 absolutio 指释放或完成。

items.en: Old French absolu carried the adjective into medieval use.
items.cn: 古法语 absolu 把这个形容词带入中世纪用法。

items.en: English extended absolute to power, proof, promises, grammar, and scientific scales.
items.cn: 英语把 absolute 扩展到权力、证据、承诺、语法与科学标度。

note.en: The first group gathers the adverb, nouns, and the same-root verb; the second gathers adjectives of completeness and lack of limit.
note.cn: 第一组收副词、名词与同根动词；第二组收表示完整与无限定的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'completely' or 'certainly'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「完全地」或「当然、绝对」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being complete or unlimited.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绝对性、完全」，指完整或无限定的性质。

entries.definition: A political system in which one ruler holds unlimited power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「专制主义」，指一人掌握无限权力的政治制度。

entries.definition: To declare someone free from blame or guilt, literally to loosen from it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「赦免、免除罪责」，字面是「把人从罪责中松开」。

entries.definition: Whole, with nothing missing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「完整的、完全的」，什么都不缺。

entries.definition: Whole and entire, often used for emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全部的、彻底的」，常用于强调。

entries.definition: Not limited by any condition or requirement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无条件的」，不受任何条件或要求限制。

entries.definition: Having no fixed limit or restriction.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无限的、不受限制的」。

entries.definition: Free from anything mixed in.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「纯粹的」，不夹杂任何东西。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin release image and the fixed collocations; the abstract hooks picture a scale without limits.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁语「释放」意象与固定搭配；抽象记忆点想象没有上限的刻度。

normal.en: Absolute and absolve share Latin absolvere, 'to loosen from'.
normal.cn: absolute 与 absolve 共享拉丁语 absolvere（从……松开）。

normal.en: Absolute silence, absolute power, and absolute zero are standard collocations.
normal.cn: absolute silence、absolute power、absolute zero 都是标准搭配。

normal.en: The adverb absolutely also means 'certainly' in conversation.
normal.cn: 副词 absolutely 在口语中也表示「当然、绝对」。

normal.en: Absolutism is the political system of unlimited rule.
normal.cn: absolutism 是无限权力的政治制度。

normal.en: In grammar, an absolute phrase is independent of the main clause.
normal.cn: 在语法中，绝对短语独立于主句。

abstract.en: Picture a gauge with no top mark, its needle still climbing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有最高刻度、指针还在上升的表盘。

abstract.en: Picture a room so silent that even the clock seems stopped.
abstract.cn: 想象房间静到连钟都像停了。

abstract.en: Picture a promise written without a single 'if'.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺里没有写任何一个「如果」。

examples.en: The task requires absolute concentration.
examples.cn: 这项任务需要绝对的专注。

examples.en: The ruler claimed absolute authority.
examples.cn: 统治者声称拥有绝对权威。

examples.en: Water freezes below a certain point on the absolute scale.
examples.cn: 水在绝对温标的某一点以下结冰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布索鲁特」——表盘上没有上限、没有条件，指针指到顶就是绝对。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ solvere（松开），过去分词 absolutus（已松开、已完成）；核心义是「摆脱一切限定、彻底完成」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from completeness and freedom from limits to unlimited power, certainty, unconditional promises, legal rights, scientific scales, and grammar.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从完整与摆脱限制，走到无限权力、确定性、无条件承诺、法律权利、科学标度与语法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gauge with no upper limit and no conditions
core.cn: 核心意象：一个没有上限也没有条件的刻度盘

branches.en: Completeness in degree: silence, beginners, and total intensity.
branches.cn: 程度上的完整：寂静、初学者与彻底的强度。

branches.en: Power and rights released from every check or condition.
branches.cn: 权力与权利摆脱一切制约或条件。

branches.en: Proof and promises that carry no doubt or condition.
branches.cn: 不带怀疑或条件的证据与承诺。

branches.en: Scientific scales fixed without a chosen reference point.
branches.cn: 不依赖选定参照点的科学标度。

branches.en: A phrase grammatically independent of the main clause.
branches.cn: 在语法上独立于主句的短语。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem absolut-, the adverb and noun endings -ly and -ness, and the political endings -ism and -ist.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 absolut-、副词与名词后缀 -ly、-ness，以及政治后缀 -ism、-ist 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin absolvere and absolutus are the direct source of absolute, so the Latin entries record the verb and its participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 absolvere 与 absolutus 是 absolute 的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其分词。

名词，义为「专制主义；绝对主义」

definition_zh: 吸收；吸进；吸引（注意）；理解；承受；并入
definition_en: to take in a liquid, gas, energy, or information, or to hold someone's attention completely
core_image: 干海绵按进水里，水被一点点吸进小孔
scene: 干沙子被倒在水洼边，水很快渗了进去。Dry sand can absorb a surprising amount of water.
sceneCN: 这里 absorb 是「吸收液体」（第 1 个义项：把外部物质吸进自身内部）；句意为干沙能吸收多得惊人的水。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「吸收；专注；合并」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「能吸收的」
由现在分词转为形容词，义为「引人入胜的」
由动词加表示物的后缀构成，义为「吸收器；吸收体」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「全神贯注的；被吸收的」

senses.title: To soak up a liquid
senses.definition: to take in a liquid or gas through pores or a surface
senses.definitionCN: 通过孔隙或表面把液体或气体吸进内部
senses.example: Dry sand can absorb a surprising amount of water.
senses.exampleCN: 干沙能吸收多得惊人的水。
senses.why: Latin absorbere meant 'to swallow up', from ab- and sorbere 'to suck in'; a sponge repeats that action.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absorbere 意为「吞下」，由 ab- 与 sorbere（吸进）构成；海绵重复的正是这个动作。

senses.title: To take in energy
senses.definition: to take in light, heat, sound, or other energy rather than reflect it
senses.definitionCN: 把光、热、声或其他能量收进去，而不是反射出去
senses.example: Dark surfaces absorb more heat than light ones.
senses.exampleCN: 深色表面比浅色表面吸收更多热量。
senses.why: The same drawing-in action applies to invisible energy, as a surface drinks light.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「吸入」动作适用于看不见的能量，就像表面把光喝进去。

senses.title: To hold attention
senses.definition: to occupy someone's attention completely
senses.definitionCN: 完全占据某人的注意力
senses.example: The film absorbed the audience from the first scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影从第一幕就吸引了观众。
senses.why: Attention is a fluid that can be drawn into a story, leaving none for anything else.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是一种可以被故事吸走的流体，别处就一点也剩不下。

senses.title: To understand and retain
senses.definition: to take in and understand information or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 把信息或观念收进来并理解
senses.example: It took time to absorb the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 理解这些新规则需要时间。
senses.why: The mind is a surface that must let knowledge soak in before it can be used.
senses.whyCN: 心智是一块必须让知识渗进去才能使用的表面。

senses.title: To take in nutrients
senses.definition: of a living body, to take nutrients into the blood or cells
senses.definitionCN: 指生物体把养分摄入血液或细胞
senses.example: The roots absorb minerals from the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 根系从土壤中吸收矿物质。
senses.why: Biology keeps the literal sense: nutrients pass from outside the body into it.
senses.whyCN: 生物学保留字面义：养分从体外进入体内。

senses.title: To bear a cost
senses.definition: to accept and deal with a cost, loss, or shock
senses.definitionCN: 接受并处理成本、损失或冲击
senses.example: The firm had to absorb the extra costs.
senses.exampleCN: 公司不得不承担额外成本。
senses.why: A cost is pictured as a blow that a strong body can take in without breaking.
senses.whyCN: 成本被想象成一击，强壮的身体能把它吸进去而不折断。

senses.title: To incorporate a group
senses.definition: to take a smaller group or area into a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 把较小的群体或地区纳入更大的整体
senses.example: The city absorbed the nearby villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市并入了附近的村庄。
senses.why: A larger body swallows a smaller one, and the smaller one becomes part of its substance.
senses.whyCN: 较大的主体吞下较小的主体，后者成为它的一部分。

senses.title: To use up time or energy
senses.definition: to take up a large part of someone's time or resources
senses.definitionCN: 占用某人很大一部分时间或资源
senses.example: The project absorbed most of her working hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目占用了她大部分工作时间。
senses.why: Time and energy are fluids that a task can drink up until little is left.
senses.whyCN: 时间与精力是会被任务喝干的流体，直到所剩无几。

intro.en: Absorb comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to swallow up', built from a prefix and the verb for sucking in.
intro.cn: absorb 来自一个意为「吞下」的拉丁语动词，由前缀与表示「吸进」的动词构成。

items.en: sorbere meant 'to suck in, swallow'; it also lies behind absorption and adsorb.
items.cn: sorbere 意为「吸进、吞下」，absorption 与 adsorb 也源自它。

items.en: ab is the preposition 'from, away', here marking movement into something.
items.cn: ab 是介词「从、离开」，此处标记向内的运动。

items.en: absorbere meant 'to swallow up, take in completely'.
items.cn: absorbere 意为「吞下、完全吸入」。

items.en: The noun absorptio named the act of swallowing up, the source of English absorption.
items.cn: 名词 absorptio 指吞没的行为，是英语 absorption 的来源。

items.en: French absorber carried the physical and figurative senses into wider use.
items.cn: 法语 absorber 把物理与比喻义带入更广的用法。

items.en: English absorb extends from liquids and energy to attention, information, costs, and the merging of groups.
items.cn: 英语 absorb 从液体与能量，扩展到注意力、信息、成本与群体合并。

note.en: The first group gathers the noun, adjectives, and device noun from the same family; the second gathers verbs for taking something in.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的名词、形容词与器具名词；第二组收表示把某物收进去的动词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning the process of taking in a substance or being engrossed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吸收；专注」，指吸入物质或全神贯注的过程。

entries.definition: An adjective or noun for a material that can take in liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「能吸收的」或「吸收材料」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning very interesting and holding attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引人入胜的」，非常有趣并吸住注意力。

entries.definition: A device or material that takes in energy or substances.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吸收器、吸收体」，指吸收能量或物质的装置或材料。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning completely engrossed in something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全神贯注的」，完全沉浸在某事中。

entries.definition: To take in a liquid gradually, as a cloth does.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「吸干、吸收」，像布料那样逐渐吸入液体。

entries.definition: To let something enter or to understand it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「吸入」或「理解」。

entries.definition: To absorb and integrate information or people into a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同化、吸收」，把信息或人纳入更大整体。

entries.definition: To occupy someone's attention completely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使全神贯注」，完全占据某人的注意力。

entries.definition: To soften the effect of a blow or cost.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缓冲、减轻」，缓和冲击或成本的影响。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the sponge image and the fixed 'be absorbed in' pattern; the abstract hooks picture liquid drawn into a surface.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用海绵意象与固定结构 be absorbed in；抽象记忆点想象液体被表面吸进去。

normal.en: Absorb and absorption share Latin sorbere, 'to suck in'.
normal.cn: absorb 与 absorption 共享拉丁语 sorbere（吸进）。

normal.en: Absorb water, absorb heat, and absorb information are standard collocations.
normal.cn: absorb water、absorb heat、absorb information 都是标准搭配。

normal.en: Be absorbed in means fully engaged, as in absorbed in a book.
normal.cn: be absorbed in 表示全神贯注，如 absorbed in a book（沉浸在书中）。

normal.en: Absorbent describes paper or cloth that takes in liquid.
normal.cn: absorbent 形容能吸液体的纸或布。

normal.en: Absorb the cost means to pay for it without passing it on.
normal.cn: absorb the cost 意为自行承担成本，不转嫁出去。

abstract.en: Picture a dry sponge swelling as water fills its tiny holes.
abstract.cn: 想象干海绵在水里胀大，细孔被水填满。

abstract.en: Picture sunlight disappearing into a black stone instead of bouncing off.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光被黑石吞进去，而不是弹回来。

abstract.en: Picture a reader so deep in a book that the room has gone quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象读者埋头书中，整个房间都安静下来。

examples.en: The soil absorbs water quickly after rain.
examples.cn: 雨后土壤很快吸收水分。

examples.en: She was completely absorbed in her work.
examples.cn: 她完全专注于自己的工作。

examples.en: The company absorbed the smaller rival.
examples.cn: 公司并吞了那家较小的对手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额布佐布」——海绵按进水里，水被小孔吸进去，外面看着还是干的。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（向内）+ sorbere（吸进），构成 absorbere（吞下）；核心义是「把外部的东西吸进内部」

sensesIntro.en: The senses all grow from 'take in': liquids, energy, attention, knowledge, nutrients, costs, smaller groups, and time are all drawn inside.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都从「吸入」生长出来：液体、能量、注意力、知识、养分、成本、较小的群体与时间，全都被收进内部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry sponge drawing water into its pores
core.cn: 核心意象：干海绵把水吸进细孔

branches.en: Physical taking in: liquids, energy, and nutrients enter a body or surface.
branches.cn: 物理上的吸入：液体、能量与养分进入物体或身体。

branches.en: Mental taking in: attention and information are drawn into the mind.
branches.cn: 心智上的吸入：注意力与信息被吸进头脑。

branches.en: A blow or cost is taken in and borne without breaking.
branches.cn: 冲击或成本被吸进去并承受住，而不致折断。

branches.en: A larger body swallows a smaller group or area.
branches.cn: 较大的主体吞并较小的群体或地区。

branches.en: Time and energy are drunk up by a task.
branches.cn: 时间与精力被任务喝干。

intro.en: The family is built from the Latin stem absorb-, the noun ending -tion, and the adjective, agent, and participle endings -ent, -er, -ing, -ed.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁词干 absorb-、名词后缀 -tion，以及形容词、施动者与分词后缀 -ent、-er、-ing、-ed 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin absorbere and absorptio are the direct source of absorb and absorption, so the Latin entries record the verb and its noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 absorbere 与 absorptio 是 absorb 与 absorption 的直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录动词及其名词。
